LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Denver is coming off a lackluster win vs. the Chargers, while Seattle looks to rebound after falling to the 49ers Getty Images In the Week 6 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Denver Broncos play host to the Seattle Seahawks . The Broncos are coming off their third win in the last four games, though it required a late, game-winning drive against the decrepit division rival Los Angeles Chargers . The return of Sean Payton as play-caller didn't exactly result in an explosive or efficient offense, but the Broncos did just enough to hold off L.A. and climb back over .500. The Seahawks, meanwhile, dropped to 3-2 after falling to their own division rivals in the San Francisco 49ers . The Niners moved the ball quite well against the vaunted Seattle defense, and turnovers in their own territory haunted the Seahawks and ultimately cost them the game. Will the Seahawks bounce back, or will the Broncos capture their second consecutive victory? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Broncos vs. Seahawks live Date: Thursday, Oct. 15 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Empower Field at Mile High (Denver) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Seahawks -2.5, O/U 40.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Seahawks have the ball Let's start here: the Seahawks cannot run the ball at all. They couldn't run the ball when rookie running back Jadarian Price was healthy earlier in the season, and they haven't been able to run the ball since he's been out. The trio of Price, Emanuel Wilson and George Holani has combined for just 447 yards on 127 carries -- an average of just 3.5 per tote. The Seahawks do not get much push up front, as their backs average a mere 0.69 yards before contact per carry, a figure that ranks fourth-worst in the NFL , according to Tru Media. Their 2.83 yards after contact per carry is more respectable, ranking 14th league-wide. The Broncos will have to be careful there. They've allowed the third-fewest rushing yards before contact per carry in the league so far (0.59), but the most rushing yards after contact (3.92), thanks to a sky-high avoided tackle rate by enemy backs (30.1%). Much of that production came from Kenneth Walker III in the season opener, but even in Weeks 2 through 5, the Broncos rank in the bottom third of the league in both yards after contact per attempt and broken tackle rate. Wilson is likely to be the primary runner once again while Price and Zach Charbonnet remain sidelined. The Broncos will have to get him on the ground on the first try, limiting the yards he can gain after contact, because the Seahawks just don't create much for him in the first place. He scarcely gets more than is blocked without breaking through tackles. In the passing game, Sam Darnold has struggled to replicate last year's results -- especially over the last two weeks. In games against the Chargers and 49ers, Darnold went just 31-of-51 for 363 yards, three touchdowns and three interceptions. After leading the league in turnovers last season, Darnold has already been picked off five times in his three full appearances this season, while his yards per attempt average is down from 8.5 to just 7.7. His completion rate is down over 3 percentage points as well. Denver's pass defense has been largely good so far this year, with the Broncos ranking fifth in opponents' EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media. The Broncos just held the Chargers to 82 net passing yards last week, which plays a huge role in that figure, but they've also allowed only one team ( Rams ) to top 218 net passing yards in any game so far. (The Chiefs didn't have to throw the ball very much in Week 1, though, because they did whatever they wanted on the ground.) The Broncos won't have Patrick Surtain II or Talanoa Hufanga here, and Riley Moss is listed as questionable -- all of which is a significant issue when you're going up against Jaxon Smith-Njigba , who leads the NFL in both receiving yards and receiving touchdowns. Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine figure to see increased roles due to the cornerback injuries, while Devon Key will play more in the wake of Hufanga's absence. They'll all have their work cut out for them against JSN. The Seahawks really don't throw the ball to anyone else all that often. When the Broncos have the ball Denver might have gotten a win last week, but Sean Payton's return as play-caller didn't have much to do with it. The Broncos entered the game against the Chargers averaging a miserable 4.9 yards per play, then averaged a mere 3.9 per play in the win over Los Angeles. Bo Nix totaled just 123 yards on his 27 pass attempts, J.K. Dobbins ran for only 68 yards on his 18 carries, Jaylen Waddle caught just two of five balls thrown his way for just 19 yards ... nothing went well offensively. And nothing has gone right pretty much all year, with the exception of the second halves of the Broncos' wins over the Jaguars and Rams in Weeks 2 and 3. Two good halves in five weeks isn't much to write home about, even if those halves helped the Broncos steal a pair of wins and arrive at 3-2. Nix is essentially refusing to push the ball down the field so far this season. His average air yards per attempt in each of his first two years of his career was 7.3, according to Tru Media, but that figure has dropped all the way to 5.2 this year. He threw deep on 13.1% of his passes as a rookie and 11.8% of them last year, but he's done so on only 7.4% of his attempts this season. Nix also isn't running anymore. He scrambled 27.3% of the time when pressured during his rookie season and 16.1% of the time last season. That number is all the way down to 5.6% so far this year, meaning he's scrambled only four times in five games. All of this, combined with his insistence on checking down repeatedly, has made the pass offense feel neutered to date. Meanwhile, the Broncos also can't run the ball. Dobbins looks like he's running with a piano on his back, slogging his way to 3.6 yards per carry. RJ Harvey barely gets opportunities, but he hasn't done any better at only 3.7 yards per carry. Harvey is at least productive in the short passing game, but the Broncos de-emphasized that last week under Payton in favor of more Dobbins runs that went nowhere. The Seahawks have largely been their usual selves defensively through the first five weeks of the season. They've arrived at their two losses largely by virtue of their offense repeatedly turning the ball over against the Commanders (three times) and 49ers (four, including a fumble that resulted in a touchdown). Seattle has held opponents to the fewest passing yards in the league and the fewest net yards per attempt, and it has limited running games to the eighth-fewest yards per attempt as well. It's hard to see the Broncos snapping out of their funk against this unit. Sean Payton's return to calling plays may have let the Broncos come away with a win, but it did not result in their offense looking competent. They averaged just 3.9 yards per play against what had previously been a very bad Chargers defense. I cannot rightly expect the Broncos to get anything going against this hellacious Seattle defense. It's not like the Broncos are going to do what the 49ers did. Denver is also still banged up defensively and likely won't have Surtain here, which is obviously a problem against JSN. Yes. Yes. Let me say it again: Yes. After a horror show in Week 4 with my NFL picks , I got back on track in a big way this past week. I was 10-4-1 straight up and 9-6-1 against the spread. That brings my season record straight up to 48-30-1 and the ATS record to 34-43-2. The ATS mark will be a slow climb to get back above .500 after that really bad Week 3. But I felt good about the picks this week. Time to build some momentum. Two good weeks in a row? All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Seattle Seahawks (-3) at Denver Broncos Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime The Seahawks lost a tough one to the 49ers last week and now face a short week on the road against Denver. The Broncos ' offense has struggled, even with Sean Payton taking over as the play-caller. Bo Nix has to pick it up, but this is a tough defense to try and fix things. Seattle takes a tough road game. Pick: Seahawks 23, Broncos 17 Houston Texans at Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) London on Sunday, 9:30 a.m. on NFL Network (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Jaguars will have been in London for two weeks, which makes this a challenge for the Texans , who went this week. Houston won for the first time on the road last week and now their division chances probably rest on this game. The Jaguars were sloppy last week, which will get them back focused. Jaguars will win a tight one. Pick: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 Chicago Bears at Atlanta Falcons (+3) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are off a horrible showing in Green Bay, in which the defense was shredded. But the Falcons lost in overtime to the Ravens and quarterback Michael Penix was hurt. He will likely play here, and that's a good thing since he can light up the Chicago defense. Falcons win it. Pick: Falcons 27, Bears 21 Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns There is a chance that Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will be back for this game after missing last week with an ankle injury. Even if he isn't, I think the Ravens defense will be up to the task of slowing down the Browns offense. If Jackson is back, the Ravens offense will move the ball. Pick: Ravens 24, Browns 13 Tennessee Titans at Indianapolis Colts (-7) The winless Titans head out on the road to play a Colts team that has been inconsistent. The Colts' defense has improved in recent weeks, which will challenge Cam Ward and the Titans' limited offense. Look for the Colts to get a division victory as Jonathan Taylor has a big game. Pick: Colts 28, Titans 17 New York Jets at New England Patriots (-7.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Patriots have turned their season around with consecutive victories as Drake Maye has come alive. The Jets played better on defense against Cleveland last week with eight sacks, but this is a bigger challenge. Look for Maye to keep it going as the Pats win a third straight. Pick: Patriots 28, Jets 13 New Orleans Saints at New York Giants (+1.5) The Saints have lost three straight and have fallen to 1-4. They didn't play well against the Vikings last week, but this is a chance to get right. The Giants tied last week, but Jameis Winston played well. I think this will be about defenses. Giants in a close one. Pick: Giants 19, Saints 16 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles (-1.5) The Panthers are off a bye, while the Eagles are off a trip to London where they lost in brutal fashion to the Jaguars. This is desperation time for the Eagles, but the injuries have piled up. Somehow, though, they will get off the deck to win this behind their defense. Pick: Eagles 23, Panthers 20 Pittsburgh Steelers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+3) Both of these teams righted the ship a bit with victories last week. The Bucs badly needed it after losing their first four. Tampa Bay ran it with Bucky Irving to beat the Cowboys and I think they can do that here as well. The defense played better in that game and will limit Aaron Rodgers somewhat. Bucs win it. Pick: Bucs 26, Steelers 21 Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Rams (-13.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The "Dream Team" Rams are 2-3 and haven't looked the part of a Super Bowl champ. The offense got it going against the Bills , but the defense was a non-factor in the fourth quarter and overtime. They will play better here against the Cardinals . Meanwhile, Matt Stafford will have a big day. Pick: Rams 35, Cardinals 20 Los Angeles Chargers (+8.5) at Kansas City Chiefs Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Chargers limp into this one at 0-5, while the Chiefs are undefeated off a bye. The Chargers are desperate and need a win or their season will be over. This is not a good place to try to get that first victory. Look for Patrick Mahomes to play well. Chiefs coach Andy Reid is outstanding in his career off a bye. Pick: Chiefs 28, Chargers 21 Buffalo Bills (-6) at Las Vegas Raiders The Bills are playing consecutive road games, but they stayed on the West Coast after beating the Rams in overtime Monday night. That was a tough, physical game, which will make it a challenge on a short week. The Raiders were awful against the Pats, but they will play better on offense here. They just won't stop the Bills. Pick: Bills 35, Raiders 21 Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers (-1.5) Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Packers blew out the Bears Sunday as Jordan Love lit up the skies. Look for more of that in this one against a bad Dallas secondary. The Cowboys struggled on defense against the Bucs, and that will continue in this one. Love continues to play well. Packers win a shootout. Pick: Packers 31, Cowboys 27 Washington Commanders at San Francisco 49ers (-7.5) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is a long road trip for the Commanders off a brutal tie last week to face the league's best team right now. That's a tough combination. They can only hope for a letdown by the 49ers after they beat Seattle last week. It won't happen. The 49ers continue to roll as Brock Purdy continues to make a claim as a legitimate MVP candidate. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict Week 6's top games Getty Images We are already in Week 6 of the NFL regular season! Can you believe it? This weekend, two AFC South rivals in the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars will battle in London, while Caleb Williams looks to return to the lineup against the Atlanta Falcons after missing the last three games. We also have an intriguing matchup in the NFC on Sunday night between the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers , while the Washington Commanders will look to get back on track against the 49ers in San Francisco following their embarrassing tie with the New York Giants . Dan Quinn needs to find a way to get his team to refocus after they completely forgot about the clock in overtime. Which teams should you pick in Week 6, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 13 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Seattle Seahawks (-2.5) at Denver Broncos (TNF) Dajani ( Seahawks -2.5): Through five weeks, I have only bet against the Denver Broncos once. It's an uncomfortable position to be in, since Bo Nix is "captain comeback." For example, I had zero doubt they would come back from down 16-0 against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 3. Denver has the most comeback wins (15), second-half comebacks (12) and fourth-quarter comebacks (8) in the NFL since 2025. However, I'm going to fade the Broncos in this spot for a couple of reasons. One, Sean Payton taking back play-calling duties did not help anything against the Los Angeles Chargers . Getting this offense off the ground is, unfortunately, going to take some time -- and it probably won't happen against the No. 1 defense in the NFL. Secondly, the Seahawks have to be mad after that loss to the 49ers. Seattle has won five straight games following a loss, having not lost back-to-back games since 2024. The Seahawks have also won seven straight prime-time games, which is the longest active streak in the NFL. … Prediction: Seahawks 23, Broncos 20 Dubin (Seahawks -2.5): Sean Payton's return to calling plays may have resulted in the Broncos coming away with a win, but it did not result in their offense looking competent. They averaged just 3.9 yards per play against what had previously been a very bad Chargers defense. I cannot rightly expect the Broncos to get anything going against this hellacious Seattle defense. It's not like the Broncos are going to do what the 49ers did. Denver is also still banged up defensively and likely won't have Patrick Surtain II here, which is obviously a problem against Jaxon Smith-Njigba . … Prediction: Seahawks 24, Broncos 16 Houston Texans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) (London) Dajani (Texans +3): The Jaguars have established themselves as one of the best teams in the AFC. While that's objectively true, they certainly aren't perfect. They probably should have dominated a short-handed Philadelphia Eagles team last week, yet didn't. Additionally, there are some questions about the offensive operation. Jacksonville went 0-3 in the red zone last week, including two trips where the Jags failed to score any points from the one-yard line. As for the Texans, they are coming off their first win of the season against the lowly Tennessee Titans . I predict they keep that momentum going and score an upset victory across the pond. DeMeco Ryans is calling defensive plays again, and C.J. Stroud is actually playing good football. He's tied for the most 20-yard completions (21) in the NFL this season. Houston is also 14-2 SU and 11-4-1 ATS in its last 16 divisional games away from home. … Prediction: Texans 21, Jaguars 18 Dubin (Jaguars -3): I think it's a real advantage that the Jaguars have already been in London for a week while the Texans haven't yet traveled across the pond. Jacksonville, as Dajani mentioned, has established itself as one of the best teams in the AFC. The offense has been efficient and explosive, and the defense has looked good as well. I know the Jags struggled with the Eagles for a bit of last week's game and probably should have lost, but Houston has only beaten a Tennessee team that is barely functional. It's not like the Texans have looked good at any point. Their defense has disappointed, and they can't run the ball whatsoever. … Prediction: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 Chicago Bears (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): It looks like Caleb Williams is going to return to the lineup after missing three games with his hamstring injury, and it also looks like Michael Penix Jr . will play after missing the very end of "Sunday Night Football" with his rib injury. The Chicago Bears have racked up their most rushing yards per contest (173.2) through five games since 1988, but keep an eye on the status of Kyle Monangai , who missed Week 5 with a toe injury. Last week's loss to the Packers was concerning from a defensive standpoint. The Bears have actually allowed 30 points over three straight road games (dating back to last year), which is tied for the longest streak in TEAM HISTORY. I'm going to take the points with the home team, and take Bijan Robinson and Co. to bounce back. … Prediction: Falcons 30, Bears 27 Dubin (Bears -3): The impending return of Caleb Williams has me leaning toward Chicago here. In the one non-monsoon game that Williams played, the Bears dropped 59 points on the Panthers . They ran the ball at will and created explosive plays in the passing game. Their defense was exposed a bit by the Packers last week, and the Falcons could get going offensively here ... if Michael Penix Jr. actually plays through the rib injury he suffered last week. At least some of this pick is thinking Tua Tagovailoa could start under center for Atlanta. … Prediction: Bears 23, Falcons 17 Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns Dajani ( Ravens -4.5): I'm not going to bash the Cleveland Browns for their loss to the New York Jets in that gross weather, where punter Corey Bojorquez missed a snap and granted the Jets 34 yards of field position to set up the game-winning touchdown. But I am nervous about Cleveland's injuries with guys like Carson Schwesinger , Mason Graham , Mike Hall Jr., Tytus Howard , Quinshon Judkins and KC Concepcion banged up. I think it's fair to say that Lamar Jackson is expected back this week after sitting one game with his ankle injury, but I was wildly impressed with this Ravens defense and their ability to shut down what was statistically the hottest offense in the NFL since Michael Penix Jr. returned. Bijan Robinson rushed for 86 yards on Sunday night. He was averaging about 170 rushing yards per game with Penix under center. If it weren't for all the walking wounded in Cleveland, I would probably side with the home dogs. Not this time. … Prediction: Ravens 26, Browns 20 Dubin (Ravens -4.5): I can't tell if this line is assuming the return of Lamar Jackson or not, but r ecent reporting suggests he has a chance to return to action . If he does, I think the Ravens win this game by a lot. The Browns might be 3-2, but they have not played like an above .500 team so far. Each of their wins required a game-winning drive late in the fourth quarter, and that's not at all sustainable. I don't trust that their offense can get anything going given the various injuries to the skill-position players, and if Jackson is back, I don't think the Ravens' offense can be stopped. … Prediction: Ravens 31, Browns 14 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles (-1.5) Dajani (Panthers +1.5): CBS Sports legend John Breech pointed out that the Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 SU and 0-3-1 ATS. That's pretty fascinating. The Eagles have covered the spread just once all season, while the last time the Panthers were on the field, they registered an impressive victory against the Detroit Lions . Bryce Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns, Chuba Hubbard rushed for 122 yards and two touchdowns and Tet McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and -- you guessed it -- two touchdowns. I have some legitimate concerns about the Panthers defense, but I'll take the upset in Philly. … Prediction: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 Dubin (Eagles -1.5): I don't feel good about this one at all. I'm basically just throwing my hands in the air and saying, well, the Eagles can't lose again , can they? … Prediction: Eagles 20, Panthers 17 Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers (-1.5) (SNF) Dajani (Packers -1.5): I told you the Packers were going to upset the Bears last week, and that something "weird" was

The defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks are coming off a loss at home to the San Francisco 49ers, dropping them to two games back of first place in the NFC West. Seattle has struggled a bit on offense, as Sam Darnold has not looked as sharp as he did last season. Darnold had a glute injury in Week 1 that sidelined him for a game, but he has started three games in a row for Seattle, leading it to a 1-2 record. Seattle still remains an elite defensive team, ranking No. 1 in the league in yards per play allowed and EPA/Play this season. The Denver defense (11th in EPA/Play and success rate) is off to a strong start as well, but the offense has lagged behind. Bo Nix is really struggling in his third NFL season, and Denver is averaging the seventh-fewest yards per play (4.7) in the NFL. Denver and Seattle both have playoff expectations – and Super Bowl hopes – in the 2026 season, but their offenses have to improve to make those dreams a reality. With Denver banged up a bit in the secondary on Thursday, Seattle has a shot to get back on track. It won’t be easy, though, as the Broncos are 2-0 at home with impressive victories against Jacksonville and the Los Angeles Rams. It's a short-week turnaround for both teams, with the Broncos coming off a win and the Seahawks off a loss. Broncos-Seahawks was the Super Bowl many people expected last season before Bo Nix's shocking ankle injury. When the 2026 schedule dropped earlier this year, this game was circled as a potential Super Bowl preview. Despite both teams sitting at 3-2, few people currently view the Broncos as a true Super Bowl contender, but that's no different than the general consensus at this time last year. The narrative around the Seahawks, though, is strikingly different. What's the disconnect? Offense. The Broncos' offense and the quality of quarterback play haven't been at a Super Bowl level — but the season is still young. How will Broncos-Seahawks shake out on Thursday night? We're going around the table to see how the Denver Broncos On SI / Mile High Huddle staff foresee this one playing out at Mile High. home.headline: Broncos Injury Report: Riley Moss questionable for Thursday Night Football, and Denver cannot afford another hit in the secondary
home.blurb: Broncos injury report: Riley Moss is questionable for Thursday Night Football vs. the Seahawks after a week of limited practice work. Moss was listed as questionable after being limited on all three Broncos practice reports ahead of Week 6. That matters because the Broncos are already without Pat Surtain II and Talanoa Hufanga, who were ruled out after being nonparticipants all week with ankle injuries. In a prime-time game at 6:15 p.m. MT on Prime Video, that is the kind of defensive personnel squeeze that can shape the entire night before the ball is even kicked. Who is available for Thursday night? The cleanest part of the Broncos injury report is that Brandon Jones, Sai'vion Jones and Ben Powers were full participants on Wednesday, and the absence of a game status means a player will be available to play. That is the good news. The less comfortable news is that Denver’s margin for error in the secondary is still thin enough to make Riley Moss the central storyline. Moss suffered the ribs injury against the 49ers in Week 4, and the Broncos have handled his week carefully ever since. The team’s first two reports of the week were estimations because it did not hold a full practice, but the final picture stayed the same: Moss limited throughout, questionable by the end, and now waiting on a decision that could matter a great deal against the Seahawks. There is a fair amount for Denver to feel better about after winning in Week 5 against the Chargers. But this is the NFL, not a therapy session. A team can enjoy a good result on one Sunday and still walk into the next game with a very real problem. Right now, the Broncos have one starting cornerback in question, two defensive backs already unavailable, and a Thursday night assignment that will expose any weakness quickly. That is not ideal. It is just the reality Denver is facing. But the numbers beneath those records leave room for a considerably less predictable afternoon in London. Jacksonville enters as a 2.5-point favorite after escaping Philadelphia 19-17. Houston finally broke through by beating Tennessee 26-3, then acquired Marvin Harrison Jr. These predictions deliberately push beyond a narrow upset or another respectable quarterback performance. The forecast: Houston produces its most complete game of the season. CJ Stroud throws for 350 yards and four touchdowns Corey Perrine/Florida Times-Union / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images Jacksonville's defense allows only 14 points per game, second in the NFL. Predicting four passing touchdowns against that unit is aggressive, but its strength against the run can obscure a vulnerable pass defense. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Jaguars surrender 277.2 passing yards per game, ranking 30th. Conversely, they allow an NFL-best 63.8 rushing yards per game and just 2.9 yards per carry. Houston therefore has good reason to attack through Stroud rather than repeatedly challenge Jacksonville's strongest area. Stroud has already thrown for 1,402 yards with six touchdowns and no interceptions through five games. Against Tennessee, he completed 26 of 34 attempts for 261 yards, including an impressive eight completions on 11 pressured throws for 115 yards. The prediction requires Houston to convert passing volume into touchdowns, something it has not consistently accomplished. Harrison's arrival creates another possible weapon, although his debut and workload remain uncertain. This call rests primarily on Stroud's existing production and Jacksonville's passing-yardage vulnerability, not an assumption that the newcomer immediately dominates. Will Anderson Jr. records four sacks as Houston forces three turnovers Anderson delivered three of Houston's four sacks against Tennessee, providing the foundation for an even bigger prediction against Jacksonville. Four sacks by one player would be a spectacular follow-up, not merely continued improvement. The Texans limited the Titans to 187 total yards and three points after DeMeco Ryans reclaimed defensive play-calling duties. Tennessee's struggling offense makes that result an imperfect measuring stick, but Houston still ranks ninth in yards allowed per play. Jacksonville presents a tougher opponent, yet Sunday exposed pressure points. Trevor Lawrence threw an interception and lost a fumble against Philadelphia despite producing 331 passing yards and two touchdowns. Houston must turn disruptive plays into possession changes, rather than simply allowing Jacksonville to reset after sacks. The Jaguars' penalty problems could help create those opportunities. They have committed at least 13 penalties and accumulated more than 100 penalty yards in consecutive games. Backward movement makes passing situations more predictable, giving Anderson additional chances to attack. The bold call is four Anderson sacks and three Houston takeaways: pressure converts Jacksonville's mistakes into decisive field-position advantages. The Texans win by at least 17 points Jacksonville's winning record and scoring defense make a comfortable Houston victory the biggest leap here. The Jaguars have allowed only 70 points across five games, while the Texans entered last Sunday without a win. Nevertheless, a blowout becomes plausible if the first two predictions connect. Houston's passing offense attacks Jacksonville's statistical weakness, while turnovers supply short fields and prevent Lawrence from answering every score. Jacksonville also needed a 53-yard kickoff return and Cam Little's 57-yard field goal to escape Philadelphia. That extraordinary finish demonstrated resilience, but it should not conceal how close the Jaguars came to losing. Stroud's four touchdown passes power the offense, and defensive disruption keeps the Jaguars from turning their rushing balance into sustained control. London delivers a division-changing upset, not another last-second escape. Harrison reunites with Stroud after their time together at Ohio State, giving the Texans another potential weapon in the passing game. Head coach DeMeco Ryans will also want his defense to maintain the intensity it showed against Tennessee. Houston limited the Titans to just three points and 187 total yards, providing an encouraging sign after a difficult opening month. Trevor Lawrence and the Jaguars Look to Continue Winning Jacksonville quarterback Trevor Lawrence leads a Jaguars offense that has helped the team build a 4-1 record. Head coach Liam Coen has Jacksonville playing competitive football, and the team's ability to find ways to win close games has been important during its early-season success. The Jaguars will look to establish their offense and take advantage of opportunities against Houston. However, Jacksonville must also adjust along the offensive line after left tackle Anton Harrison suffered a knee injury against Philadelphia. Walker Little is expected to step into the starting role, creating an important challenge against Houston's pass rush. An Important AFC South Battle Sunday's matchup gives Houston an opportunity to build on its first victory and make progress within the division. Jacksonville, meanwhile, can continue its strong start and maintain its position near the top of the AFC South. With Stroud looking to keep Houston's offense moving and Lawrence leading a Jacksonville team that has found ways to win, the London matchup offers an important test for both sides.

The Texans are coming off their first win while the Jags take the field following their most unlikely win of the season. A preseason favorite of many to contend for the Super Bowl, Houston finally got into the win column last week with an impressive 26-3 victory over the Tennessee Titans in Nashville. For the first time this season, the highly touted Texans dominated defensively, limiting Tennessee to just three points and 187 Total Yards. C.J. Stroud connected on passes to seven different receivers and threw for 261 yards to lead the attack on offense. Jacksonville, meanwhile, won a game they may not have deserved but were glad to have been gifted. They knocked off the Eagles, 19-17, at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Philadelphia took the lead with eight seconds remaining. Jacksonville was without a timeout, but Ameer Abdullah managed to return the ensuing kickoff 53 yards in seven seconds. Cam Little then converted a 57-yard field goal as time expired to win the game for the Jags. Jacksonville has now won three straight. They lead the AFC South by two games over the Colts and three games over the Texans. Stroud and the Texans have moved the ball through the air (No. 4 in the NFL with 1402 yards), but only Green Bay has gained fewer yards on the ground (No. 31 with 395 yards). Couple that disparity with an issue turning yardage into points – they have scored as a team just 11 touchdowns this season – and the 1-4 start is not all that surprising. Jacksonville’s fast start is based on the defensive side of the ball. The Jags allow yards but not points. They are the No. 2 scoring defense in the league allowing just 70 points through five games. Bottom line: Was last week’s win the start of a turnaround for Houston or will Jacksonville build on the good fortune they received last week and for all intents and purposes end the Texans’ hopes in the division? home.headline: Jaguars’ $33 Million CB Injury Update Most Concerning Among Week 6 Injury Report
home.blurb: Montaric Brown missed Wednesday's practice with a lingering hamstring issue—the same injury that sidelined him against Cincinnati and limited him to just six snaps last week. If Brown isn't cleared for Sunday, the Jaguars have no choice but to throw Travis Hunter out there for every single defensive snap, like the last two weeks. He logged 76 snaps against the Bengals and stayed on the field for all 62 defensive reps against the Eagles—plus six snaps on offense. Asking a two-way talent to anchor the secondary full-time week in and week out is playing with fire. It simply isn't a sustainable game plan, leaving him dangerously exposed to wear and tear. What's worse, there is virtually no safety net behind Hunter. With Christian Braswell out and Jourdan Lewis playing through his own ailments, the Jaguars are essentially one injury away from putting practice squad guys on the boundary against C.J. Stroud . Safety Eric Murray (concussion), right tackle Cole Van Lanen (knee), left guard Emmanuel Pregnon (toe), cornerback Jourdan Lewis (hamstring), cornerback Jaylon Jones (hamstring), cornerback Jarrian Jones (elbow), and rookie tight end Nate Boerkircher (back) did get some work Wednesday, but remained limited in practice. Harrison will have to miss at least four games, but may be out for the rest of the regular season. His timeline will be determined after the surgery. Jaguars' $33 Million CB Injury Update Most Concerning Among Week 6 Injury Report Unlock the latest Heavy on Jaguars news — direct to your inbox. Jacksonville's secondary is staring at another complete corner shuffle vs. the Texans , and the timing couldn't be worse. With Jarrian Jones , Jaylon Jones , and Jourdan Lewis all playing through injuries of their own, losing their top boundary corner leaves Anthony Campanile's defense threadbare right as Houston unleashes Marvin Harrison Jr. Montaric Brown Injury Entirely Shifts Load on Travis Hunter Jaguars Winning, But Injuries a Big Growing Concern At 4–1, the Jags are racking up wins, but Wednesday's injury report shows a locker room that's taking a beating. Injuries are standard NFL tax, but seeing a wall of red flags is a massive concern for a secondary trying to maintain a division lead. Long snapper Ross Matiscik also didn't practice Wednesday, besides Brown, as expected. Matiscik left Week 5 with a shoulder injury. Though he is not being placed on IR, the Pro Bowler is expected to miss time, and the Jaguars have signed Jacob Bobenmoyer to the practice squad and will elevate him on a game-by-game basis until Matiscik returns. The Jaguars will already be without starting left tackle Anton Harrison , who was placed on IR on Tuesday as he awaits arthroscopic knee surgery, which will reveal the extent of his injury after being carted off in last week's dramatic win over Philly . home.headline: Jaguars turn to Jacob Bobenmoyer after Ross Matiscik injury: Report
home.blurb: This story was updated to add new information. The Jacksonville Jaguars have found a replacement for defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton , who served as the team's long snapper for most of Week 5 against the Philadelphia Eagles in London. Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said Monday that the long snapper was arriving shortly, and he's now at The Grove with the rest of the team. According to NFL Media's Ian Rapoport, the Jaguars will sign veteran long snapper Jacob Bobenmoyer , while typical starting long snapper Ross Matiscik recovers from a shoulder injury sustained in the first quarter against Philly. Who is long snapper Jacob Bobenmoyer, Ross Matiscik's replacement? Bobenmoyer, 29, has spent seven years in the NFL with two teams: the Denver Broncos (2019-2022) and the Las Vegas Raiders (2023-2025). Bobenmoyer has played 97 games, recording 22 tackles and 1 fumble recovery. Jacksonville is currently overseas in London as it prepares to play its second of two matchups across the pond. The Jaguars will take on the Houston Texans in Week 6. According to Rapoport, Bobenmoyer has already flown to London. Hamilton stepped in for Jacksonville after Matiscik was injured. Teams typically carry only one long snapper on their 53-man roster or practice squad. Sunday's win marked the second time Hamilton served as the team's long snapper after Matiscik's injury. Hamilton helped set up Cam Little 's game-winning 57-yard field goal . Although Hamilton's snap was high, punter Logan Cooke got the ball down quickly, giving Little time to boot it through the uprights. The Jaguars won in the final seconds against the Eagles, 19-17. The Jaguars (4-1) will face off against the Texans in Week 6 at Wembley Stadium as they look to bury their division rival. The Texans are currently 1-4 after netting their first win over the Tennessee Titans in Week 5. Demetrius Harvey is the Jacksonville Jaguars reporter for the Florida Times-Union. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Sam Householder Thu, October 15, 2026 at 3:00 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Chicago Bears look to rebound from an ugly, humiliating loss to the Green Bay Packers while going on the road for the second straight week. This time, they should get starting QB Caleb Williams back. But he's going to have a fight on his hands. The Atlanta Falcons have an explosive offense with stars Drake London and Bijan Robinson. Robinson is making a case for being one of, if not the , best running back in the league. Certainly among elite company like Kenneth Walker III, Jahmyr Gibbs, Derrick Henry and James Cook. Michael Penix Jr., the quarterback taken seven spots after Williams, is a great facilitator for Kevin Stefanski's offense. He looks set to play despite a rib injury suffered late against the Ravens last week. Penix's biggest issue over his first three seasons has been availability. Sunday will be his 16th start and 18th overall game. Let's dive a little deeper into the Falcons and their history against Chicago. Atlanta Falcons SB Nation site : The Falcoholic Record: 2-3, second in the NFC South Last week: 30-23 loss in OT to the Ravens Game day, time, TV: Sunday, noon CT, FOX Spread: Bears -1.5 Bears all-time record against: 16-14 Historical meetings: The Bears and Falcons met in week 6 of the 2013 season with both teams at 2-3. The teams traded field goals, but Chicago found the end zone first with a 3-yard pass to Josh Morgan from Jay Cutler. This game ended up being a Bears-career high in passing yards for Cutler. He threw for 381 yards but just one touchdown. However, they had two 100-yard receiving games from Brandon Marshall (113) and Alshon Jeffery (136). Matt Forte rushed for two touchdowns. A late Matt Ryan interception helped seal it and the Bears won 27-13. Last meeting: Remember when there was very brief excitement that Matt Eberflus was building something? Week 17 of the 2023 season, the Bears moved to 7-9 when they stomped the Falcons 37-17 at Soldier Field. Taylor Heinicke threw three interceptions and was eventually benched for Desmond Ridder, who also threw a pick. Justin Fields threw a touchdown to DJ Moore, who had 159 yards. Fields also rushed for a touchdown, along with Khalil Herbert and Roschon Johnson. Herbert also had 124 yards. Injury report: The Falcons had three players on their Wednesday injury report. Did not participate CB C.J. Henderson (groin) Limited participation LB Divine Deablo (hamstring) DE Za'Darius Smith (concussion/neck) Offense: The Falcons offense ranks 13th in points and 10th in yards. Their rushing offense ranks second and their passing offense ranks 21st. The Falcons have gotten hot offensively since Michael Penix (67.5 pct. cmp./719 yds./3 TD/1 INT) came back. It helps to have Bijan Robinson (102 att./580 yds./4 TD), who leads the league in rushing. And Drake London (27 rec./488 yds./0 TD), who averages 18.1 yards per reception but somehow has no touchdowns. Bijan (18 rec./152 yds./1 TD) is actually their second-leading receiver. Followed by TE Kyle Pitts (10/109/1) and Jahan Dotson (8/149/1). Austin Hooper (5/40/1), Zachariah Branch (7/46/0) and former Bear Olamide Zaccheaus (4/17/0) are also role players. Behind Bijan is the other B. Robinson, Brian (51/210/4), who gets a fair share of carries inside the red zone. Defense: The Falcons defense ranks 21st in points and 16th in yards. Their rushing defense ranks fourth and their passing defense ranks 27th. S Xavier Watts (34 tkl/1 INT/2 PD/1 FF), LB Divine Deablo (16 tkls/1 PD/1 TFL/2 QB hits), CB Mike Hughes (25 tkls/1 TFL/3 PD) and CB C.J. Henderson (25 tkls/1 TFL/6 PD/1 FF) are the tackling leaders. S Jessie Bates III (24 tkls/2 PD/1 FR) and Za'Darius Smith (2.5 sk/4 TFL/3 QB hits) are two of the bigger names on the unit, but there is plenty of talent elsewhere, too. Cameron Thomas (2 sk/10 QB hits/1 TFL/1 FF) and Samson Ebukam (2.5 sk/9 QB hits/2 TFL) are among the leading pass-rushers. Gervon Dexter (0.5 sk/2 TFL/3 QB hits) is making himself comfortable in Atlanta's defensive scheme, too. Key matchups: The defense is going to have its hands full with Atlanta's playmakers. Bijan is tough for any team to contain. Combine him with London, who is a threat all over the field, and Dennis Allen's unit will have its hands full. Until last week's Ravens game, the Falcons have held opponents' rushing attack in check. It was opponents' aerial attacks that were doing damage. Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams will have to find the right balance to keep the Bears on the field, minimize Atlanta's time of possession, while scoring as many points as they can. The Bears can hang in a shootout, but Chicago will want the ball last. The Falcons' offense has turned the ball over in four of their five games. Atlanta has allowed nine passing touchdowns to three rushing touchdowns. The nine passing TD is tied for the fifth-most in the league. Opponents have the second-most pass attempts in the league against Atlanta, behind only Detroit. Atlanta has just one interception on the season, as well. The Falcons offense has the second-fewest pass attempts in the league and the second-most rushing attempts. While Chicago's red zone offensive woes are well-documented, Atlanta ranks seventh in offensive red zone scoring, getting in 69.2 percent of their trips.

picks.blurb: Bears vs. Falcons Preview: Chicago Looks to Bounce Back Against Atlanta - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers take 3-0 NLCS lead WNBA All-Defensive first team Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Caleb's return won't solve it all Bears vs. Falcons Preview: Chicago Looks to Bounce Back Against Atlanta Photo by: Brett Davis Stephan Stroud Thu, October 15, 2026 at 9:05 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Chicago Bears travel to Mercedes Benz Stadium on Sunday to face the Atlanta Falcons in a Week 6 matchup featuring two teams looking to respond after disappointing losses. Chicago enters the game at 3-2 after suffering a 31-7 defeat against the Green Bay Packers. Atlanta is 2-3 following a heartbreaking 30-23 overtime loss to the Baltimore Ravens. Both teams need a strong performance as they look to build momentum in their respective divisions. Kickoff is scheduled for 1 p.m. ET on FOX. Caleb Williams' Potential Return Could Boost Chicago One of the biggest storylines heading into Sunday's matchup is the status of Bears quarterback Caleb Williams . Williams has been sidelined with a hamstring injury since Week 2, leaving backup quarterback Tyson Bagent to lead the offense. Chicago struggled against Green Bay, managing only seven points in a difficult road loss. Williams' potential return could provide a major boost. His ability to extend plays, attack defenses downfield and create opportunities outside the pocket would give Chicago another dimension offensively. Running back D'Andre Swift will also be important. Swift has been a productive part of the Bears' offense, and establishing the running game could help Chicago control possession and take pressure off its quarterback. Head coach Ben Johnson will need his offense to play with greater consistency after the struggles against Green Bay. Michael Penix Jr. Leads Atlanta's Offense The Falcons also have a quarterback storyline of their own. Michael Penix Jr. is expected to return as Atlanta's starter after suffering a rib injury during the loss to Baltimore. Penix has completed 67.5% of his passes for 719 yards, three touchdowns and one interception in three starts this season. His availability will be important for an Atlanta offense that features several dangerous playmakers. Running back Bijan Robinson has been one of the Falcons' most productive players, combining explosive rushing ability with his contributions as a receiver. Wide receiver Drake London is another major threat, giving Penix a reliable target capable of making difficult catches and creating big plays. Head coach Kevin Stefanski will look to get the offense back on track after the Falcons let a late lead slip away against Baltimore. Defensive Matchups Could Decide the Game Chicago will need to contain Robinson and prevent Atlanta from controlling the game on the ground. If the Bears can force Penix into obvious passing situations, their defense could create opportunities for turnovers. Atlanta, meanwhile, must prepare for the possibility of Williams returning. The Falcons will need to pressure the quarterback while limiting Swift's opportunities to break through the defensive front. A Crucial Week 6 Test Both teams have reasons to view Sunday's matchup as an opportunity to respond. Chicago needs a better offensive performance after its loss to Green Bay, while Atlanta wants to turn its competitive play into victories. With Williams potentially returning and Penix expected to lead the Falcons, quarterback play could be the defining storyline. The team that protects the football, establishes its running game and executes in key moments will put itself in a strong position in this Week 6 showdown.

away.headline: Bears' Caleb Williams addresses online trolling of his emotional reaction to getting injured
away.blurb: Rather than the social media world being concerned about Williams and the extent of his injury, he was later trolled when the injury turned out to be a hamstring strain. "Yeah, I’m always going to show emotion, especially when I can’t be out there with the guys," Williams said. "I care about the team, the organization, winning, being out there, my teammates, all of that. I care, and that’s the biggest thing. This is what I love to do. This puts a smile on my face. It’s everything to me. So, not being able to be out there was frustrating. That was more of the tears, or whatever that was.” GM shares more bad news for Tyreek Hill about potential return to NFL amid Chiefs rumors Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams was injured in Week 2 of the NFL season, and at the time, based off his reaction, the injury appeared to be a serious one. Williams spoke to the media about the online trolling for the first time Thursday and gave clarification as to why he was so emotional leaving the field. Caleb Williams hated not being able to be on the field with his teammates When speaking to the media about the injury, Williams revealed that his emotion while being carted off the field came more from not being able to be on the field, rather than thinking he had some sort of season-ending injury. Williams also declined to give updates on his official injury diagnosis, as he told reporters that they simply did not deserve it based on the several inaccurate reports of his injuries. Will Caleb Williams be the starter in Week 6? For the first time since his injury, Williams has been a full participant in practice this week, meaning he is getting closer to returning to the field as Chicago's starting quarterback. Williams was asked if he would be the starter on Sunday, and he said he wasn't sure yet, due to still having to go through several medical procedures. Whenever he is able to make it back on the field, Williams seems to be as motivated as he ever has been. A motivated Williams with a chip on his shoulder will be a frightening thing for opposing defenses to try to stop for the remainder of the season. Want more articles like this? home.headline: Legendary Falcons' DT Grady Jarrett Returns to Atlanta With The Chicago Bears
home.blurb: Caleb's return won't solve it all On Sunday, just a week after the Falcons ' legendary defensive end, John Abraham, entered the Ring of Honor , another defensive legend will return to play against the Falcons. Defensive tackle Grady Jarrett will play his first game against his hometown and former team, the Atlanta Falcons. Until last season, Jarrett had spent his entire career in his home city of Atlanta. He was drafted out of Clemson in the fifth round in 2015. Atlanta also selected fellow defensive player linebacker Vic Beasley Jr. with the eighth overall pick. Legendary Falcons' DT Grady Jarrett Returns to Atlanta With The Chicago Bears - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL A. Noel White Thu, October 15, 2026 at 7:39 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Jarrett was seen as an undersized defensive tackle with short arms and was underestimated in his first few seasons. He grew to be a cornerstone type player, even earning his own radio call of "You shall not pass!" for his stout, defensive play and high football IQ. Jarrett was known for blowing up offensive plays through the middle of the defensive line, running down running backs for tackles for loss and, probably his most underrated skill, getting to the quarterback. For a tackle whose knock on him was short. Arms, being compared to future Hall of Fame tackle Aaron Donald , it was a major accomplishment. Part of what gave him his reputation as a quarterback hunter was his outstanding performance in Super Bowl 51 . In only his second season in the NFL, he sacked New England Patriots quarterback Tom Brady three times in the first half. That ties him for the most sacks by a player in a Super Bowl. That season, and that game in particular, put Jarrett on the map as a defensive interior lineman and into Pro Bowl conversations. Unfortunately for Jarrett and the Falcons, that Super Bowl would be the most meaningful game of his era. Unwilling to endure another rebuild or to restructure his contract, Jarrett was released in the 2025 offseason, allowing him to sign a lucrative contract with the Bears . Falcons fans used to seeing Jarrett at #97 will have to look for #50 on Sunday to give him the reception he deserves, but they also need to recognize who's terrorizing Michael Penix Jr. As much as Atlanta wants to get the win on Sunday, a great reception for Jarrett after an amazing ten years of service is to be expected.

Can you believe it? This weekend, two AFC South rivals in the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars will battle in London, while Caleb Williams looks to return to the lineup against the Atlanta Falcons after missing the last three games. We also have an intriguing matchup in the NFC on Sunday night between the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers , while the Washington Commanders will look to get back on track against the 49ers in San Francisco following their embarrassing tie with the New York Giants . Dan Quinn needs to find a way to get his team to refocus after they completely forgot about the clock in overtime. Which teams should you pick in Week 6, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 13 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Seattle Seahawks (-2.5) at Denver Broncos (TNF) Dajani ( Seahawks -2.5): Through five weeks, I have only bet against the Denver Broncos once. It's an uncomfortable position to be in, since Bo Nix is "captain comeback." For example, I had zero doubt they would come back from down 16-0 against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 3. Denver has the most comeback wins (15), second-half comebacks (12) and fourth-quarter comebacks (8) in the NFL since 2025. However, I'm going to fade the Broncos in this spot for a couple of reasons. One, Sean Payton taking back play-calling duties did not help anything against the Los Angeles Chargers . Getting this offense off the ground is, unfortunately, going to take some time -- and it probably won't happen against the No. 1 defense in the NFL. Secondly, the Seahawks have to be mad after that loss to the 49ers. Seattle has won five straight games following a loss, having not lost back-to-back games since 2024. The Seahawks have also won seven straight prime-time games, which is the longest active streak in the NFL. … Prediction: Seahawks 23, Broncos 20 Dubin (Seahawks -2.5): Sean Payton's return to calling plays may have resulted in the Broncos coming away with a win, but it did not result in their offense looking competent. They averaged just 3.9 yards per play against what had previously been a very bad Chargers defense. I cannot rightly expect the Broncos to get anything going against this hellacious Seattle defense. It's not like the Broncos are going to do what the 49ers did. Denver is also still banged up defensively and likely won't have Patrick Surtain II here, which is obviously a problem against Jaxon Smith-Njigba . … Prediction: Seahawks 24, Broncos 16 Houston Texans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) (London) Dajani (Texans +3): The Jaguars have established themselves as one of the best teams in the AFC. While that's objectively true, they certainly aren't perfect. They probably should have dominated a short-handed Philadelphia Eagles team last week, yet didn't. Additionally, there are some questions about the offensive operation. Jacksonville went 0-3 in the red zone last week, including two trips where the Jags failed to score any points from the one-yard line. As for the Texans, they are coming off their first win of the season against the lowly Tennessee Titans . I predict they keep that momentum going and score an upset victory across the pond. DeMeco Ryans is calling defensive plays again, and C.J. Stroud is actually playing good football. He's tied for the most 20-yard completions (21) in the NFL this season. Houston is also 14-2 SU and 11-4-1 ATS in its last 16 divisional games away from home. … Prediction: Texans 21, Jaguars 18 Dubin (Jaguars -3): I think it's a real advantage that the Jaguars have already been in London for a week while the Texans haven't yet traveled across the pond. Jacksonville, as Dajani mentioned, has established itself as one of the best teams in the AFC. The offense has been efficient and explosive, and the defense has looked good as well. I know the Jags struggled with the Eagles for a bit of last week's game and probably should have lost, but Houston has only beaten a Tennessee team that is barely functional. It's not like the Texans have looked good at any point. Their defense has disappointed, and they can't run the ball whatsoever. … Prediction: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 Chicago Bears (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): It looks like Caleb Williams is going to return to the lineup after missing three games with his hamstring injury, and it also looks like Michael Penix Jr . will play after missing the very end of "Sunday Night Football" with his rib injury. The Chicago Bears have racked up their most rushing yards per contest (173.2) through five games since 1988, but keep an eye on the status of Kyle Monangai , who missed Week 5 with a toe injury. Last week's loss to the Packers was concerning from a defensive standpoint. The Bears have actually allowed 30 points over three straight road games (dating back to last year), which is tied for the longest streak in TEAM HISTORY. I'm going to take the points with the home team, and take Bijan Robinson and Co. to bounce back. … Prediction: Falcons 30, Bears 27 Dubin (Bears -3): The impending return of Caleb Williams has me leaning toward Chicago here. In the one non-monsoon game that Williams played, the Bears dropped 59 points on the Panthers . They ran the ball at will and created explosive plays in the passing game. Their defense was exposed a bit by the Packers last week, and the Falcons could get going offensively here ... if Michael Penix Jr. actually plays through the rib injury he suffered last week. At least some of this pick is thinking Tua Tagovailoa could start under center for Atlanta. … Prediction: Bears 23, Falcons 17 Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns Dajani ( Ravens -4.5): I'm not going to bash the Cleveland Browns for their loss to the New York Jets in that gross weather, where punter Corey Bojorquez missed a snap and granted the Jets 34 yards of field position to set up the game-winning touchdown. But I am nervous about Cleveland's injuries with guys like Carson Schwesinger , Mason Graham , Mike Hall Jr., Tytus Howard , Quinshon Judkins and KC Concepcion banged up. I think it's fair to say that Lamar Jackson is expected back this week after sitting one game with his ankle injury, but I was wildly impressed with this Ravens defense and their ability to shut down what was statistically the hottest offense in the NFL since Michael Penix Jr. returned. Bijan Robinson rushed for 86 yards on Sunday night. He was averaging about 170 rushing yards per game with Penix under center. If it weren't for all the walking wounded in Cleveland, I would probably side with the home dogs. Not this time. … Prediction: Ravens 26, Browns 20 Dubin (Ravens -4.5): I can't tell if this line is assuming the return of Lamar Jackson or not, but r ecent reporting suggests he has a chance to return to action . If he does, I think the Ravens win this game by a lot. The Browns might be 3-2, but they have not played like an above .500 team so far. Each of their wins required a game-winning drive late in the fourth quarter, and that's not at all sustainable. I don't trust that their offense can get anything going given the various injuries to the skill-position players, and if Jackson is back, I don't think the Ravens' offense can be stopped. … Prediction: Ravens 31, Browns 14 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles (-1.5) Dajani (Panthers +1.5): CBS Sports legend John Breech pointed out that the Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 SU and 0-3-1 ATS. That's pretty fascinating. The Eagles have covered the spread just once all season, while the last time the Panthers were on the field, they registered an impressive victory against the Detroit Lions . Bryce Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns, Chuba Hubbard rushed for 122 yards and two touchdowns and Tet McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and -- you guessed it -- two touchdowns. At 4-1, Baltimore is in the driver's seat in the AFC North and has moved all the way up to +800 to win the Super Bowl. Tyler Huntley's play on Sunday night is a big reason for the Ravens' move, as he threw for 201 yards and two scores while adding 20 yards and a score on the ground. Last season, Baltimore was 0-2 in the first two games that Jackson missed with Cooper Rush taking over at quarterback, but it seems to have found something with Huntley as the backup. Baltimore has won three straight games that Huntley has started, improving the team to 7-11 all-time when Jackson is sidelined. Still, the Ravens' odds are only going to increase if Jackson plays on Sunday, and if he returns to practice in a limited fashion on Wednesday, it would bode well for his chances of suiting up. picks.headline: Lamar Jackson Injury: Oddsmakers Explain How They're Approaching Ravens vs. Browns Odds in NFL Week 6
picks.blurb: Lamar Jackson Injury: Oddsmakers Explain How They're Approaching Ravens vs. Browns Odds in NFL Week 6 Skip to main content ON SI PREDICTION MARKETS Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson did not practice on Wednesday ahead of the team’s Week 6 clash against the Cleveland Browns, putting his status in question for the AFC North rivalry matchup. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said that Jackson is “day-to-day” with the ankle injury that he suffered in Week 4 against the Tennessee Titans. Jackson did not play in the Ravens’ win over the Atlanta Falcons in Week 5, as Tyler Huntley (three total scores) led Baltimore to a victory – their third straight with him in the lineup for an injured Jackson dating back to the 2025 season. Minter said that Lamar Jackson remains “day to day” and when he’s ready, he’ll be out at practice. There has been a ton of movement in the odds for this game between the Ravens and Browns, as oddsmakers are gauging whether or not the two-time league MVP will play. Sports Illustrated spoke with several oddsmakers to give bettors some insight into how the spread for this game is currently set, and where it could move if Jackson doesn’t play. “The line this week indicates Jackson is around 60/40 to go and a revision will be made one way or the other once we know more on his status,” Johnny Avello, Director of Race and Sports Operations for DraftKings Sportsbook , told Sports Illustrated. “There were no adjustments made with the Ravens winning on Sunday night, since backups don’t usually play as well in back-to-back games as opponents have more time to prepare.” After the Ravens opened as 3.5-point favorites against the Browns on Sunday night, that line has moved quite a bit toward Baltimore. The Ravens were 4.5-point favorites early in the week and moved as far as 5.5-point favorites at home books after ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported on Wednesday that Jackson had a “realistic” chance to play against Cleveland. However, the star quarterback then missed practice, causing some books to adjust the line towards the Browns. “We're sitting at five on our site,” Ty Gour, Sports Trader at Fanatics Sportsbook , told Sports Illustrated on Wednesday. “As it currently stands as of this moment, and as Lamar's status becomes murkier, that will likely go further towards the Browns.” Still, the opening number that books shared baked in an expectation for the two-time MVP to play. Jackson’s injury isn’t considered to be a long-term issue, and he’s been one of the best quarterbacks in the NFL when he’s been able to take the field in 2026. In his four games in the 2026 campaign, Jackson has completed 70.8 percent of his passes in 2026 for 967 yards, six scores and one pick while adding 18 carries for 144 yards and a score on the ground. "Looking at this line, we are expecting Lamar to play," Christian Cipollini, Senior Trading Manager at BetMGM , told Sports Illustrated . "It will drop to under three if Lamar ends up being out. No change for Baltimore, Snoop (Huntley) is a capable backup who has similar strengths to Lamar. They do not need to change their offense when Lamar is out, which is very helpful." While BetMGM has priced Sunday’s game with the expectation that Jackson will be in the lineup, not every book has done so. FanDuel considers Jackson “questionable” in Week 6, yet it still has the Ravens as 5.5-point favorites on Thursday. “We are pricing the Browns Ravens game as if Lamar is truly questionable to play,” a FanDuel trader told Sports Illustrated. “If he is announced in/out the line will move to or away from the Ravens based on his status. Tyler Huntley's performance last week may affect this week's matchup with the Browns, but it will not change the outlook on Baltimore as a whole as their ceiling and range of outcomes is firmly tied to Lamar Jackson's health." Thursday’s practice for Baltimore will likely impact this line, as another DNP from Jackson would be a concerning sign for his chances of playing on Sunday. The Ravens are still capable of winning games with Huntley, who has completed 78.0 percent of his passes for 264 yards and two scores in 1.5 games this season. He’s also carried the ball 10 times for 36 yards and a score. Bettors that want to take the Ravens may want to wait for a more concrete update around Jackson’s status, as it seems pretty clear the betting market has set the spread for this game with the expectation that he’s more likely to play than not. picks.blurb: 3 Bold Predictions for the Browns in Week 6 against the Ravens - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers take 3-0 NLCS lead WNBA All-Defensive first team Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Caleb's return won't solve it all 3 Bold Predictions for the Browns in Week 6 against the Ravens Andrew Harbaugh, Browns Wire Wed, October 14, 2026 at 2:04 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Cleveland Browns are coming off their first loss since Week 1 as they head into Week 6. They are now 3-2 and have a pivotal matchup with the Baltimore Ravens on the horizon in what has now become a must-win game for them. The Browns can only control what they can control, and in Week 6 that is going to be more important than ever. The Ravens have been dealing with several injuries, including the most notable one regarding Lamar Jackson. Whether he plays or not, this defense needs to prepare the way they know how to. On offense, Todd Monken and Deshaun Watson have to find that spark again after losing the momentum they had been building. Without doing both of those things, this could be a major setback for the season as a whole. With that said, we have our eyes on three matchups within this game that we want to highlight. Carson Schwesinger vs. Lamar Jackson Carson Schwesinger has played at an All-Pro level this year, but he is dealing with an ankle injury. Also dealing with an ankle injury is Lamar Jackson. Neither man is likely to be 100%, so who will have the willpower to overcome the other? Schwesinger has been really flashing his pass-rush presence in 2026, which will help contain Lamar Jackson, but he also has just done a tremendous job patrolling the middle of the field. He will have to be on his A game against one of the best players of this generation. Denzel Ward vs. Zay Flowers Denzel Ward is quietly having one of the best seasons of his career, just as Zay Flowers is. The Browns cornerback has allowed an average of just 20 yards to players he is covering in 2026. On the flip side, Zay Flowers is averaging 97.3 yards per game, something has to give, right? Flowers has been pretty well contained in his career against the Browns, but every matchup is a fresh start. Whoever wins this matchup between two proverbial titans could tip the scales in their team's favor. Todd Monken vs. Jessee Minter Todd Monken will be playing against the team he left to become a head coach this offseason. He is familiar with the Ravens, Lamar Jackson, Zay Flowers, and everyone on that offense, so what will he be able to do to help Mike Rutenberg and his defense? On the flip side, Jesse Minter is looking to continue the hot start to his coaching career as the Ravens themselves are sitting pretty at 4-1. These coaches seem poised to face each other for years, but the first matchup will perhaps be the most interesting. Baltimore enters Week 6 at 4-1 after winning three consecutive games, while Cleveland sits at 3-2 and looks to protect its home field against a division rival. The Ravens are coming off a dramatic 30-23 overtime victory over the Atlanta Falcons, while the Browns are looking to respond after a difficult stretch of inconsistent performances. Sunday's game gives both teams an opportunity to strengthen their position in the division. Kickoff is scheduled for 1 p.m. ET at Huntington Bank Field, with coverage on FOX. Lamar Jackson's Status Remains Key The biggest storyline heading into Sunday's matchup is the availability of Lamar Jackson . The Ravens quarterback missed last week's game against Atlanta with an ankle injury, leaving backup Tyler Huntley to lead the offense. Huntley delivered when it mattered, helping Baltimore rally for an overtime victory and keeping the team's winning streak alive. Jackson's status remains uncertain as he works toward returning. If he is available, his mobility and ability to create explosive plays could make a significant difference against Cleveland's defense. Baltimore head coach Jesse Minter will need to prepare for both possibilities while ensuring the offense maintains its rhythm. Running back Derrick Henry will also be a major factor. Henry has been one of the league's most productive runners, and his physical running style gives Baltimore a reliable option regardless of who starts at quarterback. Deshaun Watson Leads Cleveland Cleveland quarterback Deshaun Watson will look to take advantage of the opportunity to challenge Baltimore's defense. Watson has shown flashes of productivity this season, but the Browns need more consistency from their passing attack. Wide receiver Denzel Boston and tight end Harold Fannin Jr. have provided important targets, giving Cleveland options to stretch the field and move the chains. First-year head coach Todd Monken knows Baltimore well after previously serving as the Ravens' offensive coordinator. That familiarity adds another storyline to Sunday's contest, although Cleveland's biggest priority will be executing its own game plan. The Browns also need to establish the running game to prevent Baltimore from focusing entirely on Watson and the passing attack. A Crucial AFC North Battle The Ravens have won three straight meetings with Cleveland and enter Sunday's game with momentum. However, the Browns have an opportunity to make a statement at home against a division rival. Baltimore will look to maintain its offensive balance and continue its winning streak, while Cleveland needs a complete performance on both sides of the ball. With Jackson's availability still a major question and Henry providing a powerful presence in the backfield, the Ravens have several ways to attack Cleveland. The Browns will need disciplined defense and more consistent offensive production to keep pace. Sunday's matchup could have an important impact on the AFC North race as both teams continue their push through the 2026 season.

away.headline: Zay Flowers, Mike Green added to Ravens' Thursday injury report
away.blurb: The Ravens added Zay Flowers and Mike Green to their injury report Thursday, while Lamar Jackson remained sidelined ahead of Sunday's AFC North matchup against the Browns . Flowers was listed as limited with a toe injury, and Green with a hamstring injury. Neither appeared on Wednesday's report, giving Baltimore two additional situations to monitor before its trip to Cleveland. Jackson was listed as a nonparticipant for the second consecutive day with an ankle injury. Rashod Bateman (shoulder), John Simpson (groin), and Broderick Washington (ankle) moved from limited participation Wednesday to nonparticipation Thursday. Tight end Matthew Hibner remained a nonparticipant with a hand injury. Jackson's absence keeps Tyler Huntley in line for another start if the two-time MVP cannot return. Coach Jesse Minter has said Jackson could play without practicing, and Thursday's report does not establish his game status. There were encouraging developments elsewhere. Marlon Humphrey (hamstring/calf), Roger Rosengarten (knee), Ronnie Stanley (rest/toe/ankle) and Nick Vannett (knee) improved from limited to full participation. Calais Campbell also returned to full participation following Wednesday's rest day. Trey Hendrickson (finger), Kyle Hamilton (stinger), Mark Andrews (hand) and Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) remained full participants. Lane is designated to return from injured reserve; full participation alone does not establish that he has been activated. Center Cam Jurgens remained limited with a concussion as he works toward his Ravens debut. Teddye Buchanan, Emery Jones Jr., Trenton Simpson and Andrew Vorhees also remained limited. Baltimore enters Sunday at 4-1, one game ahead of Cleveland. Friday's practice and game designations will help determine whether the Ravens can get Jackson back and how many of their other injured players will be available for the division matchup. away.headline: Ravens Linked to Dolphins' Former 11.5-Sack Edge Rusher as Baltimore's Pass Rush Stalls at 10 Sacks
away.blurb: Baltimore’s sacks have been spread thin. Tavius Robinson leads the team with three, Mike Green has two, and Hendrickson had one in three games before the injury. Green had his best day in the overtime win at Atlanta, with a sack, two quarterback hits and two tackles for loss, but no Ravens rusher has more than three sacks. Head coach Jesse Minter sounded hopeful Monday that his top edge rusher could return against the Browns. Trey Hendrickson’s Potential Return Could Be Disastrous For Browns Offensive Line The Baltimore Ravens are 4-1 and atop the AFC North, but they’ve gotten there without much heat on opposing quarterbacks. With Trey Hendrickson sidelined by a finger injury the last two weeks, Bleacher Report’s Alex Kay pointed Baltimore toward a pass rusher who once had 11.5 sacks in a season: Miami Dolphins edge Josh Uche. Kay proposed sending a 2027 sixth-round pick to the winless Dolphins for Uche in his one trade for each of the NFL’s best teams . He noted that the Ravens are generating pressure on about 20.2% of plays, with a 5.52% sack rate and 10 sacks through five games. Josh Uche is playing like a starter again Uche’s best year came with the Patriots in 2022, when he had 11.5 sacks. He bounced from New England to Kansas City to Philadelphia over the next three seasons before signing a one-year deal in Miami, and he’s been productive there. PFF grades Uche 33rd of 106 edge defenders with a 71.7 overall mark, and he has 10 pressures on 111 pass-rush snaps. He also has 20 tackles, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery. “I think Trey will be chomping at the bit to be ready to roll this week,” Minter said during his Monday news conference . Even with Hendrickson back, Uche would give Baltimore another rusher to rotate in. The cost is minimal. He’s on a one-year, $1.4 million deal with a $1.215 million base salary, and the Ravens have about $2.4 million in cap space, per Over the Cap . For a team that wants M&T Bank Stadium rocking in January, a sixth-round pick for a 28-year-old rusher is an easy call to make before the Nov. 10 deadline. away.headline: Ravens Coach Jesse Minter Gives Lamar Jackson Update Before Browns Game
away.blurb: Head coach Jesse Minter gave an update on the two-time NFL MVP on Wednesday, offering encouragement without committing to his return. Minter also praised Jackson's efforts to get back on the field, making it clear that the quarterback is working toward a return. "To Lamar's credit, he's working his butt off, he's doing everything he can to be out here and, when he's able to be, then he will," Minter said. Jackson's likely return would be significant for Baltimore's offense. His ability to threaten defenses as both a passer and a runner makes him central to the Ravens' attack, particularly alongside running back Derrick Henry. The Baltimore Ravens could receive a major boost ahead of their Week 6 matchup against the Cleveland Browns, but Lamar Jackson's availability remains uncertain as the team monitors his ankle injury. Jackson has not practiced since suffering the injury during Baltimore's Oct. 4 win over the Tennessee Titans. "Sure, yeah, I think, it's definitely day to day," Minter said, per the Ravens' official video. "I think a lot of times those things right when they happen you're not sure, and as you gather information, you look at stuff," he added. There is some reason for optimism.
