However, his lack of participation in Wednesday's practice means the Ravens still need to evaluate his progress before making a decision. If Jackson cannot play, Tyler Huntley is expected to start again after leading Baltimore to an overtime victory over the Atlanta Falcons in Week 5. Huntley helped the Ravens secure the win, keeping them competitive despite losing their starting quarterback.

home.headline: Jets' Minkah Fitzpatrick Fined by NFL for Illegal Hit That Injured Browns' KC Concepcion
home.blurb: Concepcion exited the game following the hit and was later ruled out due to a head injury . For more from Bleacher Report, check out our B/R app , homepage and social feeds—including Twitter , Instagram , Facebook , TikTok and YouTube . New York Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick received a fine from the NFL for his hit on Cleveland Browns wide receiver KC Concepcion during a Week 5 matchup between the two teams. In the first quarter of the game, Concepcion was hit hard by Fitzpatrick as he attempted to haul in a pass from Deshaun Watson. Fitzpatrick was flagged for unnecessary roughness on the play. The Jets ended up winning the contest by the final score of 17-12. This article will be updated soon to provide more information and analysis.

home.headline: Lamar Jackson Injury Update, Latest Rumors on Ravens QB's Status for NFL Week 6 vs. Browns
home.blurb: Jackson has a "realistic chance to return for Sunday's game at Cleveland," ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Wednesday. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter later told reporters that Jackson is considered day-to-day. Minter added that Jackson is "working his butt off" and "doing everything he can" to return to the field. Jackson was out for Week 5 as Tyler Huntley led the Ravens to an overtime win at the Atlanta Falcons. Bleacher Report • 2h Jalen Hurts Out Sunday Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson could be back on the field in time for a Week 6 matchup against the Cleveland Browns. Pats Open AJ's Practice Window He initially left Week 4's 24-18 win over the Tennessee Titans with an ankle injury and didn't play in the second half, a concerning development for a Ravens' offense very much reliant on the dynamic quarterback's unique skill set. ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported the Ravens are "hopeful" Trey Hendrickson—who has missed two games with a thumb injury—returns this week. While the Ravens didn't believe at the time that Jackson's injury was going to be a long-term issue, there was uncertainty over his short-term availability. "I really don't think it's going to be crazy long term, but we'll see what happens," head coach Jesse Minter told reporters at the time. There's no replacing a two-time MVP and three-time first-team All-Pro like Jackson, though the Ravens do have an experienced backup in Huntley. "There's one Lamar Jackson, the guy's a two-time MVP," Minter said after Week 4. "And so I think for anybody to have to say we're being compared to Lamar is unfair and not realistic. I think [Huntley] as a backup quarterback in this league and even as a starter at times has shown the ability to come in and really kind of run the offense, make plays with his legs, be able to make plays on third down." Injuries were also a concern for Jackson last season, as he missed four games due to a hamstring injury and a back contusion. Huntley started two of those games, leading the team to a 2-0 record. home.headline: Wednesday injury report for the Browns Week 6 against the Ravens
home.blurb: Caleb's return won't solve it all Coming off a tough road loss to the New York Jets, the Cleveland Browns return home to Huntington Bank Field for a pivotal AFC North clash against the Baltimore Ravens . However, the initial Week 6 injury report paints a grim picture for Cleveland's health, as a staggering 11 players sat out Wednesday's session, leaving the roster severely depleted on both sides of the ball. The offensive line and backfield took massive hits as well, with starting tailback Quinshon Judkins, backup Dylan Sampson, right tackle Tytus Howard, and backup guard Teven Jenkins all sitting out. There is a slight glimmer of hope among the limited group, particularly in the receiving room, as wide receiver Tylan Wallace returned to practice in a limited capacity after missing multiple weeks. He was joined by Denzel Boston and rookie KC Concepcion, who is working through concussion protocol. On defense and the offensive line, safety Grant Delpit and center Elgton Jenkins were both managed with limited workloads. Gilberto Manzano , NFL Staff Writer Iain MacMillan , Senior Editor, Betting Peter Dewey , Associate Managing Editor, Betting All odds listed are via DraftKings Sportsbook Gilberto Manzano Week 6 Upset Pick Houston Texans (+120) vs. Jacksonville Jaguars First, let me pat myself on the back for finally getting an upset pick correctly. Now that I’ve regained your trust after my Packers-over-Bears pick came to fruition last week, do yourself a favor and take the new-look Texans over the London Jaguars. Houston gained confidence from beating up on Tennessee and landing wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. in a trade with Arizona. C.J. Stroud tends to play at his best when Nico Collins is on the field, but now he doesn’t have to lock in on him with the arrival of Harrison, who played with Stroud at Ohio State. More importantly, the Texans’ defense is back on track, and that could present trouble for the inconsistent Trevor Lawrence. Iain MacMillan Week 6 Upset Pick Tennessee Titans (+260) vs. Indianapolis Colts It's time for the Titans to get their first win of the season. You might be surprised to find out how many metrics these two teams rank similarly in, even some that the Titans outrank the Colts in, like net yards per play, which has the Titans at -0.7 and the Colts second-last in the NFL at -1.6. Another interesting metric for this game is that the Titans have the second-highest run frequency in neutral game states, meaning on early downs in the middle of the game when they still have a more than 20% win probability, Tennessee loves to run the football. That could be an area they exploit in this game, as the Colts rank dead last in the NFL in opponent rush EPA and 30th in opponent run success rate. Meanwhile, the Titans rank 16th and 11th in those two run defense categories, which will go a long way in slowing down Jonathan Taylor, which is the key to beating this Colts team. I'll take Tennessee as my upset pick of the week. Peter Dewey Week 6 Upset Pick Carolina Panthers (-105) vs. Philadelphia Eagles This isn’t the craziest upset pick in Week 6 – Carolina is just a 1.5-point underdog – but I can’t pass up a chance to fade this Philadelphia offense. Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith are dealing with soft-tissue injuries, and the Eagles currently rank 30th in EPA/Play, 31st in success rate and 31st in yards per play this season. Only the Tennessee Titans (0-5) are averaging fewer yards per play than Philly. I think there’s a real chance that Bryce Young and this Carolina offense (eighth in EPA/Play, sixth in EPA/Pass and fifth in yards per play) put up too many points for this Eagles team to compete. After all, the Eagles are 17th in yards per play allowed on defense and 22nd in both EPA/Play and success rate. Both of those advanced numbers are behind the Panthers’ defense this season. If the Eagles didn’t enter the season with playoff expectations, I think they’d be underdogs on Sunday based on their statistical profile in 2026. Plus, Carolina is coming off a bye while the Eagles have a tough travel week coming from London. All signs point to a Panthers upset in Week 6. But divisional games rarely follow a predictable script, and the Colts have plenty to prove as they look to build on their iffy start to the season. With another week of football ahead, here are four bold predictions for Sunday's matchup in Nashville. Red Zone Struggles Will Continue Through the first five games, the Colts red zone offense has been ultra-reliable. Now, the Titans (0-5, 0-1 AFC South) are a seven-point underdog before its divisional road game against the Indianapolis Colts (2-3, 1-0) at Lucas Oil Stadium on Oct. 18 (noon CT, FOX). The Colts are one of four teams with losing records remaining on the Titans' schedule. It doesn't seem right to circle those games as easy opportunities for coach Robert Saleh, considering the Texans were 0-4 when they blitzed the Titans. Quarterback Cam Ward and Tennessee's best chances will be against sub-.500 teams. But even that has been a struggle in a weak AFC South. Nas 0728 Titans Camp 003 | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Jon Spradley Mon, October 12, 2026 at 11:01 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Indianapolis Colts are picking up divisional play in Week 6 against the Tennessee Titans. It's a welcomed return home after a road trip that produced mixed results. After traveling to London and collecting a win, things went sideways in Pittsburgh. FanDuel Sportsbook is giving the Colts the edge against the winless Titans with a 6.5-point spread advantage. The money line is at -330 with the over/under starting at 43.5. The Colts did what they do; they lost in Pittsburgh. Unable to finish drives and giving up huge plays on defense was the story of the afternoon. After going up 3-0, they never regained the lead. Every time the Colts got close, they had to settle for 3. Luckily, Spencer Schrader was on his game, but it wasn't enough. An 80 and 50 yard score by Jaylen Warren was too much to overcome as the Colts fell, once again, to the Steelers in Pittsburgh. The Titans and Texans were entrenched in the battle of the winless as one team would get off the schneid and the other would sink further down. Cam Ward and the Titans might really be that bad. They scored the first 3 but then allowed the Texans to rattle off the next 26. Jobs might be on the line as the season is quickly slipping down the drain. Lose again and the Titans might be eyeing a replacement for Ward in the draft with the No. 1 pick. The Colts have work to do, but the Titans might be the best remedy to what ails them. Nothing is certain, but this is a great opportunity to get to 3-3 and finish the first third of the season at .500. Finding the end zone and putting up 6 in place of 3 is a great place to start. The Colts can do it, but they have plenty to tighten up before then.

picks.headline: Titans vs. Colts Preview: Indianapolis Looks to Bounce Back Against Winless Tennessee
picks.blurb: Titans vs. Colts Preview: Indianapolis Looks to Bounce Back Against Winless Tennessee - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers take 3-0 NLCS lead WNBA All-Defensive first team Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Caleb's return won't solve it all Photo by: Charles LeClaire Stephan Stroud Thu, October 15, 2026 at 9:13 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Tennessee Titans travel to Lucas Oil Stadium on Sunday to face the Indianapolis Colts in an AFC South matchup featuring two teams with very different starts to the 2026 NFL season. Tennessee enters Week 6 at 0-5 after suffering a disappointing 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans. Indianapolis is 2-3 following a 34-22 defeat against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Both teams are looking to respond, but the Titans desperately need their first victory of the season. Kickoff is scheduled for 1 p.m. ET on FOX. Cam Ward Looks to Spark Tennessee's Offense Titans quarterback Cam Ward remains the centerpiece of Tennessee's rebuilding effort. Despite the team's winless start, head coach Robert Saleh has continued to express confidence in the young quarterback and his ability to develop. Ward has completed 63.2% of his passes for 896 yards, three touchdowns and three interceptions through five games. However, the Titans have struggled to generate consistent offense, scoring just three points against Houston last week. Tennessee needs Ward to make quicker decisions, protect the football and find ways to connect with his receivers downfield. Running back Tony Pollard will also be important. Establishing a productive ground game could take pressure off Ward and help Tennessee control possession against Indianapolis. Daniel Jones and Jonathan Taylor Lead Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones will look to guide Indianapolis back into the win column after the loss to Pittsburgh. Jones has thrown for 1,021 yards and three touchdowns this season, although four interceptions have contributed to some of the team's offensive inconsistency. Against Tennessee, protecting the football and taking advantage of scoring opportunities will be essential. The Colts also have one of the league's most dangerous running backs in Jonathan Taylor . Taylor has recorded 398 rushing yards and six touchdowns through five games, giving Indianapolis a reliable option to control the tempo. Wide receiver Josh Downs and tight end Tyler Warren provide Jones with additional receiving threats. Head coach Shane Steichen will look to create a balanced offensive attack that allows Taylor to establish the run while opening opportunities for Jones through the air. Can Tennessee Slow Down the Colts? The Titans' defense must find a way to contain Taylor and prevent Indianapolis from controlling the line of scrimmage. If Tennessee allows the Colts to establish their rushing attack early, Ward could face additional pressure to produce points quickly. Indianapolis, meanwhile, will try to pressure Ward into difficult decisions and capitalize on turnovers. A Crucial AFC South Battle Sunday presents an important opportunity for both teams. Tennessee is searching for its first win, while Indianapolis needs a response after consecutive losses. The Titans will need a more productive offensive performance from Ward, while the Colts will look to Taylor and Jones to lead the way. With both teams eager to get back on track, execution and ball security could determine the outcome of this divisional matchup.

away.blurb: Tennessee Titans cornerback Cor'Dale Flott (chest) will not return in Week 5's game against the Houston Texans . Safety Isaiah Oliver, who was elevated from the practice squad this week, collided with Flott on an incomplete pass late in the second quarter. Flott returned for stretches before leaving permanently. Micah Robinson played in Flott's absence and was beaten for a 9-yard touchdown by Houston's Jaylin Noel early in the fourth quarter as the Texans upped their lead to 26-3. Start the day smarter. Offensive lineman Matt Goncalves and rookie defensive end Jaylahn Tuimoloau were both limited Wednesday after leaving practice to undergo concussion evaluations. Outside of Josh Downs, there just haven't been many sparks from this group. Downs leads the healthy receivers with 20 catches for 249 yards, but he appeared on Wednesday's report as limited with rest/hamstring listed. Keenan Allen did not practice due to rest, while Ashton Dulin remained sidelined with a hamstring injury. One encouraging development was Darius Slayton returning as a full participant after a knee injury kept him out against Pittsburgh. Jonathan Taylor was limited strictly for rest, while Charvarius Ward also received a rest day. Tight end Will Mallory was another full participant as he continues working toward a potential return from injured reserve. Colts Open Week 6 With Several Key Names on Injury Report Skip to main content SI.COM At this point, Indianapolis Colts fans are probably tired of watching injuries take a toll on this roster. It feels like the same story we've seen over the last decade-plus, and through five weeks of the 2026 season, injuries are once again making life considerably more difficult for Indianapolis. Wednesday's injury report featured several notable names, including two players who left practice for concussion evaluations. And for a team sitting at 2-3, the last thing Indianapolis needs is more injuries to important contributors. Two Important Colts Undergo Concussion Evaluations Whether either player passed those evaluations remains unclear, but both situations deserve attention heading into Sunday. Goncalves has been a valuable piece of the offensive line, and with Daniel Jones already struggling to find consistency, losing another contributor up front certainly wouldn't help. Tuimoloau's situation might be even more frustrating considering the current state of Indianapolis' defensive line. With Arden Key recently landing on injured reserve, Indianapolis needs its younger pass rushers to step up and produce . Potentially losing another body along the defensive front would only make that challenge more difficult. Linebacker Jaylon Carlies also missed practice with the rib injury that sidelined him against Pittsburgh. Considering how poorly this linebacker room has performed through five weeks, Indianapolis can hardly afford another week without one of its starters. home.headline: Germaine Pratt aiming to bring leadership, stability to defense in second go-around with Colts
home.blurb: The Colts are seeking consistency at linebacker, with snaps divided in Week 5 between Akeem Davis-Gaither (52 snaps), Austin Ajiake (32 snaps), CJ Allen (24 snaps) and Bryce Boettcher (11 snaps) with starting WILL linebacker Jaylon Carlies (ribs) out. As with Davis-Gaither, the Colts see value in Pratt's experience not only in the NFL, but with Anarumo's system. Germaine Pratt aiming to bring leadership, stability to defense in second go-around with Colts Skip to main content Primary nav SCHEDULE The Colts signed the 30-year-old Pratt, who started 12 games for them in 2025, to their practice squad on Tuesday. While Germaine Pratt went unsigned up until Tuesday, he found a way to still be involved in football. The 30-year-old veteran linebacker spent time in the summer as a volunteer coach at North Carolina State , where he worked with his alma mater's linebackers. He eventually had a tryout with the Dallas Cowboys, though he didn't sign. This week, Pratt got his chance to get back into playing instead of coaching. The Colts signed him to their practice squad on Tuesday, and while it's too early to tell if and when he'll make his 2026 debut, Pratt said his goal is to use his experience to bring leadership to the Colts' linebacker room. "Helping the defense, just being in this system for so long, that's all I know," Pratt said. "So help it stabilize and settle it down, make tackles, whatever the case may be, get some turnovers." Pratt has played all but four of his 112 NFL games for Lou Anarumo, his defensive coordinator with the Cincinnati Bengals (2019-2024) and Colts (2025). In 2025, Pratt signed with the Colts in October after being released by the Las Vegas Raiders and started 12 games, totaling 101 tackles, a forced fumble and an interception. The experienced WILL linebacker has had over 100 tackles with at least one interception and one forced fumble every year since 2023. "Just adding a veteran presence is big in there," head coach Shane Steichen said. "He's played a lot of football in this league, made a lot of plays, and any time you can add good players to your roster, you want to do that." In the immediate future, whether Pratt could factor into that group on Sunday against the Tennessee Titans – he'd have to be elevated to the active roster from the practice squad – remains to be seen given he didn't participate in training camp and took the field for his first practice of the 2026 season on Wednesday. "I don't know the plan," Pratt said. home.blurb: Colts sign TE Pharaoh Brown to 53-man roster from practice squad, sign LB Germaine Pratt to practice squad Skip to main content Primary nav SCHEDULE The Colts made the roster move on Tuesday. The Indianapolis Colts today signed tight end Pharaoh Brown to the 53-man roster from the practice squad. The team also signed linebacker Germaine Pratt to the practice squad. Brown , 6-5, 246 pounds, has spent the entire season on the team's practice squad. He has played in 94 career games (56 starts) in his time with the Colts (2026, 2023), Arizona Cardinals (2025), Miami Dolphins (2025), Seattle Seahawks (2024), New England Patriots (2023), Cleveland Browns (2018-20, 2022), Houston Texans (2020-22) and Oakland Raiders (2017-18). Brown has compiled 74 receptions for 752 yards (10.2 avg.) and three touchdowns. Pratt , 6-3, 250 pounds, re-joins Indianapolis after spending time with the team last season. He has started 104-of-112 career games in his time with the Colts (2025), Las Vegas Raiders (2025) and Cincinnati Bengals (2019-24) and has totaled 734 tackles (416 solo), 38.0 tackles for loss, 3.5 sacks, 33 passes defensed, eight interceptions, eight forced fumbles, seven fumble recoveries and eight special teams stops. Pratt has started seven postseason contests and has compiled 49 tackles (32 solo), 1.0 tackle for loss, four passes defensed and one interception. In 2025, he started 12 games with Indianapolis and registered 101 tackles (57 solo), 5.0 tackles for loss, eight passes defensed, one interception, one forced fumble and two fumble recoveries. The Dallas Cowboys entered Thursday night’s showdown with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers as 9.5-point favorites, yet they lost outright at home, destroying plenty of Survivor entries in the process. Week 5 had three teams that were obvious Survivor selections: Dallas, Houston and Cincinnati. They were all playing 0-4 teams, but only the Bengals and Texans came through. Luckily for the SI Betting team, neither of our editors selected the Cowboys this week, meaning that if you tailed our picks , you’re still alive heading into Week 6. Bye weeks are really starting to come into play in Survivor, as the Detroit Lions, Minnesota Vikings, Miami Dolphins and Bengals all won’t play in Week 6. One of the best strategies in Survivor this season has been fading the 0-5 Dolphins, so players will have to look elsewhere on Sunday. There are still some huge favorites in Week 6, the Los Angeles Rams are favored by double digits at home against the Arizona Cardinals, and the Kansas City Chiefs, Indianapolis Colts and New England Patriots are all favored by at least a touchdown at home. Each week, the SI Betting team of Iain MacMillan and Peter Dewey makes their favorite Survivor selections each week to help guide our readers through the season. Here’s a recap of our Week 5 selections before we dive into our favorite Survivor teams in Week 6. NFL Week 5 Survivor Picks Recap Peter Dewey: Cincinnati Bengals (W) Iain MacMillan: Houston Texans (W) Both Dewey and MacMillan faded winless teams in Week 5, and both wins were relatively sweat free with the Texans blowing out Tennessee and Cincy cruising to a big lead in a seven-point win over Miami. There are still plenty of playoff contenders that we can choose from in Week 6, even in just a 14-game slate. Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook NFL Week 6 Survivor Pool Picks Indianapolis Colts Indianapolis is going to be a popular pick in Survivor this week because it’s playing the Titans, but I’m willing to take a shot on Daniel Jones and company to get back to .500 at 3-3, especially at home. Indy is currently a seven-point favorite against the worst team in the AFC South. Cam Ward and the Titans have been downright awful on offense, ranking dead last in yards per play, 31st in EPA/Play and 26th in success rate during their 0-5 start. They’ve scored 20 or fewer points in every game, including three games where they scored 10 or less points. Indianapolis hasn’t done a great job of finishing drives this season, but it has one of the best kickers in the NFL in Spencer Shrader. So, Indy is able to get enough points on the board (like it did in Week 5) even if it doesn’t score a bunch of touchdowns. The Colts are allowing the third-most yards per play in the NFL on defense, which is a concern for them when it comes to this pick. However, Tennessee is 2-8 on the road in the Ward era, and it has covered the spread in just four of those games. The Indy offense isn’t a juggernaut, but it has moved the ball a lot better than the Titans, hanging 30 points on the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 2 while ranking 21st in success rate and 22nd in EPA/Play. I don’t see many spots where I’d willingly take the Colts in Survivor, so this is a way to use them and hopefully advance to Week 7. With more bye weeks ahead, it’s important to save a few top teams – if possible – for a game that may not be as much of a sure thing. Indy at home against the Titans is by far the most favorable game on the team’s schedule outside of a Nov. 15 home game against Miami. The Titans have been lost to open this season, and I don’t expect them to turn things around any time soon with how abysmal their offense has looked. The Colts may not cover, but they should handle business at home in Week 6. – Peter Dewey New England Patriots The New England Patriots proved last week that they still can show flashes of the team that won the AFC last season, especially when they play the weaker teams in the NFL. Their defense is a top 10 unit and Drake Maye can still torch a below average secondary. The Patriots now rank 10th in EPA per play, while the New York Jets rank 20th. New England is also 11th in opponent success rate, while New York is 23rd. That could all lead to big things for the Patriots in this divisional game. The Patriots have a ton of tough games on their schedule this season, including the Detroit Lions, Buffalo Bills, Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos, so taking them when they're at home against either the Jets or Dolphins is going to be the move, which is why this is the week I'll take them at Gillette Stadium against Geno Smith and Aaron Glenn. Plus, New England is 18-2 at home in its last 20 games against the Jets. – Iain MacMillan Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. Bill Ervolino shares your pain News Bergen Sports HS Sports Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals JETS NY Jets vs Patriots expert picks and predictions for Week 6 game Albert Bainbridge IV Art Stapleton Bob Jordan Mike Dougherty Chris Iseman Brian Marron Dave Rivera NorthJersey.com Oct. 14, 2026, 6:03 a.m. ET After their worst performance of the young NFL season in Week 4, it was a complete 180 by the New York Jets in Week 5. Their defense was relentless all day as No. 2 overall pick David Bailey had a career day with three sacks in the Jets' 17-12 win over the Cleveland Browns at MetLife Stadium last Sunday. Jets RB Braelon Allen − who has started for injured star running back Breece Hall the last two games − scored the game-winning touchdown with three minutes left in regulation. The victory snapped a three-game losing streak for the Jets after opening the season with a road victory over the Tennessee Titans . It'll be tough for the Jets to replicate their performance in Week 6, as they head on the road to take on the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium, a house of horrors for Gang Green over the past 15 years. The Jets have lost 14 of their last 15 games in New England, with the lone exception being a 17-3 win during the final week of the 2023 season on Jan. 7, 2024. Our NFL prognosticators are: Art Stapleton ( Giants /NFL writer, NorthJersey.com), Bert Bainbridge (sports trending reporter/columnist, NorthJersey.com), Brian Marron (digital producer, NorthJersey.com), Chris Iseman (Rutgers writer, NorthJersey.com), Mike Dougherty (sports writer, lohud.com), Bob Jordan (sports editor, Asbury Park Press/APP.com) and Dave Rivera (sports editor, USA TODAY Northeast/NorthJersey.com). Jets vs Patriots Week 6 staff predictions, staff standings Brian Marron: 5-0 Dave Rivera: 5-0 Art Stapleton: 4-1 Bert Bainbridge: 4-1 Bob Jordan: 4-1 Mike Dougherty: 4-1 Chris Iseman : 3-2 Will the Jets pull off the upset in Foxborough? Here are our staff predictions for this AFC East battle on Sunday: Bert Bainbridge The pick: Patriots 31, Jets 13 Here's why: The Jets defense stepped up to the challenge in Week 5, but they'll face a much more difficult test on the road against a Patriots offense that's heating up after a slow start to the season. New England puts this divisional contest out of reach in the second half. Art Stapleton The pick: Patriots 27, Jets 17 Here's why: The Jets are catching the Patriots at the wrong time. Two weeks ago, Drake Maye was lost and the league was talking about his struggles. Now, after wins over the Bills and the Raiders , Maye is lighting it up. He's a different quarterback than Deshaun Watson, so don't expect Aaron Glenn's defense to have similar success. The pick: Patriots 40, Jets 17 Here's why: When the Patriots struggled to a 1-2 start, it looked like this could be a game where the Jets could extract more payback for that recent 15-game losing streak in this series. Oh well. The pick: Patriots 27, Jets 16 Here's why: The Jets are facing Drake Maye and the Patriots at the wrong time as New England is starting to get on a roll. It won't be a blowout, but the Patriots will play from ahead throughout the game. Mike Dougherty The pick: Patriots 30, Jets 17 Here's why: Drake Maye is no longer playing like a lost soul. He threw four TD passes last week against the Raiders and regained the complete trust of a sneaky good offensive group. The Jets simply don't have enough playmakers on that side of the ball to keep up. Drake Maye and the resurgent Patriots will not provide the Jets with the same gifts. The pick: Patriots 34, Jets 13 Here's why: No way the Jets are winning two games in a row. away.headline: Two key Browns players leave Week 5 against the Jets with injuries

away.headline: New York Jets' Blitz Rate Is a Risk Against Patriots QB Drake Maye
away.blurb: The potential return of Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown (ankle) raises the stakes. Locked On Patriots host Nick Cattles said Brown had returned to practice after the team opened his 21-day window, though his availability and workload remained unclear. Butchko said Brown’s presence would force the Jets to alter their coverage approach even if he plays a limited role because New York lacks the true shutdown corner it once had with Sauce Gardner. – Tight end Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) returned to practice in a limited capacity, according to Butchko. He argued the Jets need to simplify the rookie’s role and create more intermediate-field opportunities if he is cleared, particularly with Breece Hall and Adonai Mitchell expected to miss the game. The New York Jets may need to abandon the volume of defensive pressure that helped them beat Cleveland when they visit the New England Patriots on Sunday. Locked On Jets host John Butchko pointed to New York’s blitz rate in Week 5 and argued that repeatedly sending extra rushers at Patriots quarterback Drake Maye would leave the Jets liable to big plays. (Butchko referred to the blitz rate as 47%, but TruMedia listed it as 52.3%.) Butchko said Maye’s mobility and success against pressure make this a different assignment from the rain-soaked matchup against the Browns. The Jets can still create a turnover by disguising pressure and picking their spots, but an overemphasis on the blitz would give Maye chances to extend plays and attack openings in the secondary. A more selective rush would put greater responsibility on the secondary to cover longer, especially if Brown is active. The Jets have received better-than-expected early contributions from cornerbacks Azareye’h Thomas and Brandon Stephens, plus safety Dane Belton, but Maye presents a more demanding test when he can escape the initial pressure. The counterargument is clear: Sitting back too often could give Maye a clean pocket and allow the Patriots to sustain their explosive-play offense. New York’s answer may be to vary its looks rather than make pressure the defining feature of every passing down. For a defense that has protected its red zone well, preventing a few vertical completions could matter more than chasing sacks. The Jets have a path to a second straight win if they make Maye work through tight windows, limit the Patriots’ explosive plays and avoid letting one coverage bust turn an aggressive call into a momentum swing. – Wide receiver Garrett Wilson will draw a major individual test from Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez (shoulder), who returned to practice after missing the past two games. Butchko said New York’s depleted receiver group leaves little margin if Gonzalez can limit Wilson’s targets. Some or all of this content may have been generated by AI. away.headline: New York Jets secondary expects Patriots and Drake Maye to severely test them through the air
away.blurb: Fortunately for the Jets, safeties Minkah Fitzpatrick, Dane Belton and Andre Cisco form a strong unit that can deliver punishing hits. Receivers going across the middle will have to keep their eyes open, lest they suffer the type of hit that put Cleveland rookie KC Concepcion out of the game in Week 5. The Pats are also hoping to see something from A.J. Brown, who has been out but returned to practice this week. If he’s activated for the game, he’ll be used to test Stephens on vertical shots down the field. A.J. Brown being out with ankle injury has forced the Patriots to look for ways around the star receiver’s absence. The Pats say his participation will be a game-time decision. The New York Jets secondary faces a heavy test this week against the New England Patriots. While the Jets defense has won a lot of kudos, particularly for the defense’s sack attack, they face a different beast in the Patriots. Quarterback Drake Maye and head coach Mike Vrabel know how to mount an air attack, and will be poised to probe the weakest spots of the Jets secondary. Cornerback Brandon Stephens figures to be a particular target. Second-year corner Azareye’h Thomas has been so solid that teams are largely staying away from him, which puts the pressure on Stephens to cover his side of the field. The Jets frequently blitz, so the secondary is typically used for tight, physical coverage. Slot corner Jarvis Brownlee Jr., a frequent blitzer, also ranks near the top of the NFL in tackle efficiency among defensive backs. New England is expected to use tight ends Hunter Henry and Austin Hooper in two tight-end formations. Drake Maye will try to offset the Jets pressure by taking short drops and short passes, a tactic that has worked several times for other teams. That means linebackers Demario Davis and Jamien Sherwood will have to make their presence felt. New England beat up the Las Vegas Raiders last week, as Drake Maye threw for 374 yards and four touchdowns. Receiver DeMario Douglas played a major part in that, catching two scores. He will be deployed against Brandon Stephens, who will be tested early. If the Jets get too comfortable defending the pass, the Patriots will look to their ground game to loosen things up. The goal is to force hesitation, which will open things up in the intermediate range. New England frequently deploys heavier personnel on the field. The Patriots hope to force the Jets to stay in standard base defenses or compromise their nickel packages. If the Jets try to over-index on stopping the run, Maye has shown he can take advantage in the middle. The Patriots can punish teams who leave safeties in a single-high look. Maye was 4-6 for 149 yards and two touchdowns on throws over 20 yards against the Raiders. They may test the Jets at some point in similar fashion.

By Matt Audilet Contributing Sports Writer 0 Share Newsweek is a Trust Project member See more of our trusted coverage when you search. Prefer Newsweek on Google to see more of our trusted coverage when you search. New England Patriots starting left tackle Will Campbell suffered a knee injury during this past Sunday's Week 5 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. Campbell underwent MRI testing to determine the severity of his injury on Monday. And according to a report from NFL insider Tom Pelissero, the 22-year-old offensive lineman avoided a serious, long-term injury. Campbell is now considered "week-to-week" as the Patriots prepare for this coming Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the division-rival New York Jets. “We’ll see how the week goes,” Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said of Campbell's injury status on Monday. “It’ll get looked at and continues to rehab. Wasn’t able to finish the game, so I don’t know how much time he’ll miss — if he’ll be back towards the end of the week, if he’ll be back Wednesday. We’ll take it day by day and see how he feels tomorrow, see what he does Wednesday, and keep you updated on the injury report.” After a slow start to the 2026 season, the Patriots are beginning to catch their stride. Sunday's 45-17 win over the Raiders marked the team's second consecutive victory and third win of the season thus far. Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the Jets will kick off at 1 p.m. ET.

The second-year quarterback has shown the ability to make plays through the air, but the Saints have struggled to find consistency during their recent losing streak. Through five games, Shough has thrown for 1,299 yards, nine touchdowns and five interceptions. He will need to make smart decisions and avoid turnovers against a Giants defense that has shown it can pressure opposing quarterbacks. Wide receiver Chris Olave remains one of New Orleans' most important offensive weapons. His ability to create separation and make plays downfield could be crucial as the Saints try to stretch the Giants' defense. Running back Alvin Kamara is another key player to watch. Establishing a productive rushing attack would help New Orleans create a more balanced offense and prevent New York from focusing primarily on Shough and the passing game. Head coach Kellen Moore needs his team to execute more consistently after the Saints managed just 142 total yards against Minnesota. Jameis Winston and the Giants Look to Build Momentum The Giants enter Sunday's game with confidence after rallying from a 14-point fourth-quarter deficit against Washington before settling for a tie. Quarterback Jameis Winston has stepped into the starting role and helped spark the offense. Against Washington, Winston led the Giants to 24 points on their four full drives in the third and fourth quarters, giving New York a chance to complete the comeback. The Giants also have playmakers capable of creating problems for New Orleans. Wide receiver Malik Nabers gives Winston a dangerous target, while tight end Isaiah Likely provides another option in the passing game. Harbaugh has emphasized his team's resilience, and the Giants will look to carry that mentality into their return home. A Key Matchup in the Trenches One of the biggest factors could be New York's pass rush against New Orleans' offensive line. If the Giants consistently pressure Shough, the Saints could struggle to sustain drives. New Orleans, meanwhile, needs its defense to contain Winston and prevent the Giants from producing the explosive plays that helped fuel their comeback last week. What to Watch Sunday The Saints need a complete performance to end their losing streak, while the Giants have an opportunity to strengthen their position in the NFC East. With Shough trying to steady New Orleans' offense and Winston leading a resilient Giants team, quarterback play and execution on third down could be decisive in this Week 6 matchup.

(Photo by Derick Hingle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Caleb Yaccarino Wed, October 14, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads I want to start this week's report by talking about this class. Like many, I have seen it ranked very low on lists of the best and worst classes from 2026. I don't disagree with those lists, and really, who can? Injuries, players being behind veterans, or some still needing to develop have kept this class from doing much, but you shouldn't lose faith in this group. The players who have been in the game have made plays that are good starting points, and although development matters, it's not like those players have been bad. Jordyn Tyson's injury is annoying to say the least, but hopefully we can forget about that once he's back. Do I think this class is going to be like 2025? No, but in hindsight, I think he could be a nice, middle-of-the-road draft class. Now onto the players: DT Christen Miller Finally, Christen Miller was able to get into the game on Sunday, and eventhough the Saints could not win, he did well in his short time. Miller made big plays against the run, took up blocks from offensive linemen to open up holes for other defensive linemen and the linebackers to stop the run, and in my opinion, proved he should be the starting nose tackle. It wasn't perfect, but it was enough for the Saints to play him more. This should hopefully be the case against the New York Giants, and to stop RB Cam Skattebo, you need a big defensive lineman that can prevent him from carrying the pile. TE Oscar Delp With the Vikings sending blitzes nearly every play, Delp had to step up as a blocker, and he did. The Giants are also at the top of the league in blitz rate, so Delp will be a primary blocker once again. I do hope the Saints utilize him as a receiver, because Noah Fant has had pre-snap issues this season, and prioritizing youth should be the plan moving forward. Try something new. OG Jeremiah Wright Speaking of trying something new, I wish Jeremiah Wright would get some snaps, but now that pressure is on the organization to win, a Cesar Ruiz trade feels less likely due to the risk. If a coaching change is made, I hope the next staff will give Wright a chance. WR Bryce Lance Last week, I said that it's clear Lance is not ready for WR3, and the Vikings game only reinforced that. The Saints need to make the move and put him at WR4 moving forward so he can learn. I know I have said to prioritize youth, but I also want to prioritize Tyler Shough's development, and Lance is negatively affecting that. WR Barion Brown Brown is a similar spot to Lance, but it's also clear he needs to figure out the return game as well. His fellow former LSU Tiger, Zavion Thomas, is in nearly the exact same spot with the Bears, but due to their offensive struggles with Caleb Williams being out, they have begun to utilize Thomas more. In addition, Thomas has improved as their main return man. Hopefully, the same can happen for Brown. RB CJ Donaldson Donaldson was thrown to the wolves trying to block the Vikings blitz, and although I felt he did a decent job, he did have a holding call on one of the plays. As a rusher, Donaldson did exactly what I thought, picking up tough yards that did help the Saints in their run game. Against the Giants, I want him to be included once again. OT Mason Murphy In probably the most confusing moment of the game, which is saying a lot, the Saints put in Mason Murphy on a random drive, then subbed him out for Asim Richards the next. At first, I thought Richards got injured, but Moore said after the game that it was planned. I actually thought Richards did better than usual, and Murphy wasn't great when he came in. I don't think the Saints will make this substitution again. DB Lorenzo Styles Jr. Styles Jr. was back last game, which was nice to see, but his involvement was limited. I wouldn't be shocked if that changes after Jayden Price's release being cut, so Styles Jr. could be the return man next to Brown against the Giants. Injured players: WR Jordyn Tyson

While this “foot” designation could be cause for concern, the fact that Olave took the field for a limited practice is a positive sign for his Week 5 status. New Orleans Saints wide receiver Chris Olave did not participate in Wednesday’s Week 5 practice session, landing on the injury report with a “rest” designation. This new issue comes as a surprise to fans and reporters who saw Olave take a hit to the knee late in Monday night’s matchup against the Atlanta Falcons. Trailing 45-17 with just over one minute remaining in the primetime contest, the superstar wide receiver limped off the field with what was assumed to be a knee injury. Olave ranks second in NFL receiving yards so far this season with 491, trailing only Dallas Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb (498). He recorded his third 100+ receiving yard game of the year in Monday’s loss to the Falcons, reeling in eight receptions for 116 yards. Chris Olave continues to raise concern this week on the New Orleans Saints ‘ injury report. That remains true in Week 6 as the Saints prepare to play at the new York Giants . This time around, it's actually a bit more concerning with the latest update on Thursday. Chris Olave Injury, Illness Update Olave missed practice entirely for a second consecutive day on Thursday. He's listed with an illness, the same thing he was listed with on Wednesday. It feels like somewhat often, an NFL player will miss one day of practice with an illness. Two days in a row is a lot less common, and it raises at least a little doubt about whether Olave will play in Week 6. Olave has played in all five games this season and been really good for the Saints as their No. 1 wide receiver. He caught 10 passes for 182 yards in Week 1. In Week 2, it was eight catches for 86 yards and a touchdown. His Week 3 stats were nine catches for 107 yards. Then in Week 4, Olave went for eight catches and 116 yards. In each of the first four weeks, he had double-digit targets. Olave cooled down a bit in Week 5, catching 4-of-6 targets for 46 yards. If he were to miss a game, Devaughn Vele would become the No. 1 WR, with rookie Bryce Lance as the No. 2. An Olave absence would also likely result in more 2-TE sets with Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant on the field at the same time. At this point, Friday's injury report will be the most useful information yet. An illness is different from an injury in that a player could likely simply get over it in a day. Carter has 2.0 sacks, and is tied sixth in the NFL among edge defenders and linebackers with 14 quarterback pressures. Carter leads the league with 11 ‘quick’ quarterback pressures, defined as pressures achieved in less than 2.5 seconds. If Eluemunor cannot play, Marcus Mbow would start at right tackle and rookie J.C. Davis would be the swing tackle. Safety Jason Pinnock, who missed last week’s game due to a concussion, was a full practice participant. That is good news, especially with Nubin trending toward not playing.

home.headline: NY Giants can’t ask two young tackles to save them alone
home.blurb: The Giants had neither starting offensive tackle at Wednesday's practice. Andrew Thomas was out with a groin issue, Jermaine Eluemunor with a calf injury, and John Harbaugh identified Marcus Mbow and J.C. Davis as the next options. Neither starter has been ruled out for Sunday. New York still needs a contingency plan that asks more of the coaches than putting two inexperienced tackles in the same protections and hoping Jameis Winston survives the difference. Thomas and Eluemunor's absences appeared on the first Week 6 injury report . A Wednesday DNP isn't a forecast of the final game status. It is enough reason to prepare for a less comfortable situation than the one on the preferred depth chart. A sensible early-down passing plan can reduce the number of obvious long-yardage dropbacks. Mix in throws Winston can get out on time, keep the run available when the situation supports it, and choose the deeper attempts rather than asking a replacement tackle to win a long one-on-one assignment over and over. NY Giants can't ask two young tackles to save them alone Opens in a new tab Giants The Giants' backups have very different experience Mbow has three career NFL starts, all from last season. He has appeared in each of the first five games this year without starting. Davis is a rookie whose official record lists no regular-season appearances yet. Calling both players young is accurate; treating their preparation as interchangeable would ignore a meaningful difference. Harbaugh praised their work in his Wednesday remarks . He didn't announce a final starting combination for the Saints game, and the Giants haven't supplied enough public information to assign each backup a definite side in a possible two-replacement lineup. My preference would be a small, rehearsed set of protection adjustments for whichever replacement is needed. That can mean a chip before a back releases, a tight end helping before entering the route, or a protection slide that gives the most difficult matchup another blocker. Each option has a cost. Holding a player in protection removes an immediate receiving option. Sliding help one way can leave somebody else isolated. The point isn't to keep everybody near the quarterback on every snap. It's to make those choices before the defense forces a panicked correction. What do you think? Post a comment. Protection shouldn't become an excuse to stop attacking That proposal isn't a report of the Giants' private game plan. We also don't have the evidence to say Mbow or Davis requires constant help. If practice and the game show either can hold up, the coaches should release more receivers and use the full offense. New Orleans is 1-4 entering Sunday at MetLife Stadium, but that record doesn't block a pass rusher. I'd rather see the Giants prepare the assistance and discover they need less of it than wait for repeated pressure to admit the assignments were too demanding. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Tyler Sullivan picks every game on the Week 6 schedule, including five locks against the spread Getty Images I don't know what it is about the Week 6 slate, but I think we're going to have some underdogs bark rather loudly. I have four underdogs not only finding their way into my five locks of the week, but also two of them pulling off outright upsets. Judging by the headline of this article, you already know that the Panthers are one of those dogs that I think will win in Week 6 as they head up to Philly to face the Eagles . While I'll get into why I feel that way below, I'm just as fascinated by what may happen if it comes to fruition. Would this be the straw that breaks the camel's back when it comes to Nick Sirianni's job? Or does he live to fight another day and gear up for a do-or-die NFC East showdown in primetime with the Cowboys in Week 7? Either way, the storylines that could flow out of this upcoming slate feel like they're as juicy as we've seen so far this season, and that's saying something. Anyways, I'll look to improve upon my picks after a lackluster Week 5 where I went 2-3 ATS with my five locks of the week, along with 6-9 ATS and 9-5-1 SU for the overall slate. Note : Cincinnati, Detroit, Miami and Minnesota are on the bye in Week 6. Locks of the Week ATS : 12-12-1 ATS : 33-44-2 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles Sunday, 1 p.m. (CBS, Stream on Paramount+ ) Carolina comes into this matchup with a pretty sizable rest advantage over Philadelphia. On top of the Panthers coming off of the bye, the Eagles were just in London last week. So, we have one team extremely well rested, while the other is reeling and just came off a demoralizing international loss. Beyond the lopsided rest advantage, the Eagles just feel like a mess right now. They're bottom five in the league in points per game (18.4), yards per game (262.2), and passing yards per game (170.6) coming into Week 6. Sure, some of that can be attributed to injury, but even when they've had their full squad, it's been clunky. Conversely, Carolina's offense is top-five in the NFL in those same categories, and it looks like they'll get No. 2 wideout Jalen Coker back for this one. I like the Panthers to roll into Lincoln Financial Field and turn the heat up under Nick Sirianni's seat to a fever pitch. Projected score: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 The pick: Panthers +1.5 Pittsburgh Steelers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers This is another game that has some outliers worth targeting. The Bucs will be at home after an upset win over the Cowboys last Thursday night in Dallas. They'll have the rest advantage over a Steelers team that took care of business against the Colts on Sunday. Similar to how I think the Cowboys sort of overlooked the then-winless Buccaneers with an undrafted rookie quarterback under center, Pittsburgh could get caught sleeping here, too. Not so much because they're going to overlook Jalon Daniels , but the Steelers could get caught looking ahead to their Week 7 matchup against the Saints in Paris. With a France trip on the horizon for Pittsburgh, I think Tampa Bay is a live home dog. Moreover, I think the Bucs defense has a good shot at containing the Steelers offense. Tampa Bay is allowing the second-fewest rushing yards per game in the NFL through Week 5, which could limit Jaylen Warren's impact. Meanwhile, Todd Bowles has some solid splits against Aaron Rodgers over the course of his career as both a head coach and defensive coordinator. Rodgers' teams are 1-2 against Bowles and average just 16.7 points per game. Projected score: Buccaneers 24, Steelers 23 The pick: Buccaneers +3 Tennessee Titans at Indianapolis Colts Sunday, 1 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free) You'll undoubtedly scratch your head at this pick, and it's hard to blame you. Tennessee hasn't instilled any confidence this season and is punting on a league-high 53% of its drives. Still, I think this line is too big in a divisional matchup against the Colts, whom I don't believe are a serious player in the AFC. The Indy offense can't move the ball efficiently, ranking 29th in the NFL in yards per play (4.6). Meanwhile, their defense is 28th in the league in total yards allowed (384.2). Daniel Jones has also turned the ball over more times (7) than he's found the end zone (4) this season. So, for as bad as the Titans offense has been this season, Indy isn't that far off, so I'll gladly put the full touchdown in my back pocket. Projected score: Colts 24, Titans 20 The pick: Titans +7 Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free) I think we're firmly on backdoor alert with this line. L.A. is coming off an overtime loss to the Bills on Monday night, so this is quite the turnaround for Sean McVay's club. Matthew Stafford dropped back and threw 54 times in the loss, while the Rams offense ran 78 total plays. That could see them a bit sluggish in this contest. I don't envision Arizona pulling off the upset, but I do think they're capable of scoring late to get us within the number here. For instance, Arizona kept the offense on the field throughout a blowout loss to Detroit and scored a largely meaningless touchdown just before the two-minute warning. That's the type of play we'll be looking for them here. Projected score: Rams 30, Cardinals 17 The pick: Cardinals +13.5 New York Jets at New England Patriots I think the Patriots are all the way back. Drake Maye has seemingly returned to his MVP form from last year and just tallied five touchdowns in a blowout win over the Raiders . Gillette Stadium has been a comfortable spot for New England as they're 10-1 in their last 11 home games. Meanwhile, they've also taken care of business against inferior opponents under Mike Vrabel as the Patriots are 11-0 with him at the helm when facing teams entering with a losing record. Further looking at the trends for this one, the Patriots are 12-0 straight-up and 10-2 ATS in their last 12 games as a favorite and have a +17.9 PPG differential over that stretch. As for the Jets , they've yet to win or cover (0-6) a divisional game under head coach Aaron Glenn. He isn't changing his ways this week, either, picking the Eagles to win by three despite giving ample reason the Panthers should win. Quarterback Jalen Hurts is the latest player to go down, as he's been diagnosed with a superficial blood clot and will not play in Week 6 against the Carolina Panthers. Hurts apparently played with the clot in his calf on Sunday against the Jacksonville Jaguars, but the team decided to rule him out for this week after an ultra sound revaled movement in the clot. pic.twitter.com/9SeK1XzYRL Losing Hurts has impacted the Eagles' odds for Week 6 against the Panthers, as they are now home underdogs of more than a field goal. picks.blurb: Panthers vs. Eagles Preview: Carolina Looks to Take Advantage of Philadelphia’s Struggles - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers take 3-0 NLCS lead WNBA All-Defensive first team Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Caleb's return won't solve it all Photo by: Bob Donnan Stephan Stroud Thu, October 15, 2026 at 7:57 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Carolina Panthers travel to Philadelphia on Sunday for an important Week 6 matchup against the Eagles, with both teams looking to get their seasons moving in the right direction. Carolina enters the game at 2-2 following a bye week, while Philadelphia sits at 2-3 after suffering three consecutive losses. The Eagles are coming off a heartbreaking 17-16 defeat against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London, where a late field goal sealed another frustrating result. Kickoff is scheduled for 1 p.m. ET at Lincoln Financial Field, with the game airing on CBS. Bryce Young Leads Carolina's Offense Panthers quarterback Bryce Young will be one of the biggest players to watch Sunday. Young has shown significant improvement during the 2026 season, helping Carolina develop a more productive passing attack. His connection with rookie wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan has become an important part of the offense, giving the Panthers a dangerous combination through the air. Carolina's offense looked particularly effective in its victory over the Detroit Lions before the bye week. Young will look to carry that momentum into Philadelphia against an Eagles defense that has struggled to consistently close out games. Head coach Dave Canales will also want to establish the running game and keep Young in manageable situations. If Carolina can maintain balance offensively, it could create opportunities to attack Philadelphia downfield. Tanner McKee Takes Over for Philadelphia Philadelphia faces a significant challenge at quarterback after Jalen Hurts was ruled out because of a superficial blood clot in his leg. Backup Tanner McKee is expected to start in his place. McKee has limited NFL starting experience, making Sunday's matchup an important opportunity for him to demonstrate what he can do against Carolina's defense. Head coach Nick Sirianni will need to put McKee in favorable situations while finding ways to generate offense despite the team's recent struggles. Philadelphia's offensive line has also undergone significant changes, and the Eagles have struggled to establish their usual rushing attack. Getting the running game going could help take pressure off McKee and allow the offense to find a rhythm. An Important NFC Matchup For Carolina, Sunday's game represents an opportunity to take advantage of an Eagles team dealing with several challenges and return from the bye with a statement victory. Philadelphia desperately needs to stop its losing streak and regain confidence at home. With Young leading Carolina's offense and McKee stepping into a starting role for the Eagles, execution and turnovers could play major roles in determining the outcome. Both teams have plenty to prove, making Sunday's matchup an important test for their respective seasons.

Eagles Week 5 injury tracker: Full details on every player out for Philly The Philadelphia Eagles are hoping to bounce back in Week 6 as they face the Carolina Panthers. Philly is coming off a 19-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in London, falling to a last-second field goal. Carolina didn't play last week because it was their bye week. The running game only had 22 yards last week, and the passing game is inconsistent at best. It doesn't help that the offensive line has struggled all season with lineup changes and more happening. Jalen Hurts is the star of the offense and the man who has to carry the team on his back, potentially without Barkley and Smith. In Week 5, Hurts showed he might not be perfect at it, but he can do it. He needs to do it more consistently and use his legs to pick up yards. Eagles' defense faces off against a top-ranked passing attack Before their bye week, Bryce Young was leading the NFL in passing yards. The Panthers are dangerous in the passing game, led by rising star receiver Tetairoa McMillan. Quinyon Mitchell got his first career regular-season interception last week after four in the postseason so that the Eagles will need more of that. home.headline: Eagles injury report: DeVonta Smith was limited, Saquon Barkley sits
home.blurb: DeVonta Smith returned to limited participation Thursday, giving the Eagles an encouraging development as they prepare to face Carolina without Jalen Hurts . Smith, who is dealing with hamstring and toe injuries, was listed as a nonparticipant Wednesday before improving Thursday. Saquon Barkley remained a nonparticipant with a hamstring injury, joining six other Eagles who did not practice. Hurts was listed as a nonparticipant with a calf injury after Philadelphia ruled him out against the Panthers because of a superficial blood clot. The Eagles also practiced without Michael Carter II (abdomen), A.J. Epenesa (back), Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle), Will Shipley (foot) and Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring). Wicks and Epenesa went from limited participation Wednesday to nonparticipants Thursday. Wicks' status adds another concern for a passing game already preparing for a quarterback change, making Smith's progress particularly important. There were improvements elsewhere. Drew Kendall (knee) returned to limited participation after missing Wednesday's session, while Marcus Epps (groin) advanced from limited to full participation. Landon Dickerson (knee), Jakorian Bennett (knee), Grant Calcaterra (back) and Eli Stowers (quad) remained limited after Wednesday opened their practice windows. Their participation does not mean they have been activated from injured reserve. Marquise Brown (ankle), Jonathan Greenard (ankle), E.J. Jenkins (toe) and Tyler Steen (shoulder) also remained limited. Barkley's continued absence leaves Philadelphia waiting on its depleted backfield. Tank Bigsby is on injured reserve, and Shipley's foot injury has created another opening for Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele if Barkley cannot return. Smith's limited participation is a step forward, but his availability for Sunday remains unsettled. Friday's practice and the final injury report will clarify who will be available around Philadelphia's replacement quarterback. The Broncos ' offense has struggled, even with Sean Payton taking over as the play-caller. Bo Nix has to pick it up, but this is a tough defense to try and fix things. Seattle takes a tough road game. Pick: Seahawks 23, Broncos 17 Houston Texans at Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) London on Sunday, 9:30 a.m. on NFL Network (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Jaguars will have been in London for two weeks, which makes this a challenge for the Texans , who went this week. Houston won for the first time on the road last week and now their division chances probably rest on this game. The Jaguars were sloppy last week, which will get them back focused. Jaguars will win a tight one. Pick: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 Chicago Bears at Atlanta Falcons (+3) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are off a horrible showing in Green Bay, in which the defense was shredded. But the Falcons lost in overtime to the Ravens and quarterback Michael Penix was hurt. He will likely play here, and that's a good thing since he can light up the Chicago defense. Falcons win it. Pick: Falcons 27, Bears 21 Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns There is a chance that Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will be back for this game after missing last week with an ankle injury. Even if he isn't, I think the Ravens defense will be up to the task of slowing down the Browns offense. If Jackson is back, the Ravens offense will move the ball. Pick: Ravens 24, Browns 13 Tennessee Titans at Indianapolis Colts (-7) The winless Titans head out on the road to play a Colts team that has been inconsistent. The Colts' defense has improved in recent weeks, which will challenge Cam Ward and the Titans' limited offense. Look for the Colts to get a division victory as Jonathan Taylor has a big game. Pick: Colts 28, Titans 17 New York Jets at New England Patriots (-7.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Patriots have turned their season around with consecutive victories as Drake Maye has come alive. The Jets played better on defense against Cleveland last week with eight sacks, but this is a bigger challenge. Look for Maye to keep it going as the Pats win a third straight. Pick: Patriots 28, Jets 13 New Orleans Saints at New York Giants (+1.5) The Saints have lost three straight and have fallen to 1-4. They didn't play well against the Vikings last week, but this is a chance to get right. The Giants tied last week, but Jameis Winston played well. I think this will be about defenses. Giants in a close one. Pick: Giants 19, Saints 16 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles (-1.5) The Panthers are off a bye, while the Eagles are off a trip to London where they lost in brutal fashion to the Jaguars. This is desperation time for the Eagles, but the injuries have piled up. Somehow, though, they will get off the deck to win this behind their defense. Pick: Eagles 23, Panthers 20 Pittsburgh Steelers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+3) Both of these teams righted the ship a bit with victories last week. The Bucs badly needed it after losing their first four. Tampa Bay ran it with Bucky Irving to beat the Cowboys and I think they can do that here as well. The defense played better in that game and will limit Aaron Rodgers somewhat. Bucs win it. Pick: Bucs 26, Steelers 21 Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Rams (-13.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The "Dream Team" Rams are 2-3 and haven't looked the part of a Super Bowl champ. The offense got it going against the Bills , but the defense was a non-factor in the fourth quarter and overtime. They will play better here against the Cardinals . Meanwhile, Matt Stafford will have a big day. Pick: Rams 35, Cardinals 20 Los Angeles Chargers (+8.5) at Kansas City Chiefs Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Chargers limp into this one at 0-5, while the Chiefs are undefeated off a bye. The Chargers are desperate and need a win or their season will be over. This is not a good place to try to get that first victory. Look for Patrick Mahomes to play well. Chiefs coach Andy Reid is outstanding in his career off a bye. Pick: Chiefs 28, Chargers 21 Buffalo Bills (-6) at Las Vegas Raiders The Bills are playing consecutive road games, but they stayed on the West Coast after beating the Rams in overtime Monday night. That was a tough, physical game, which will make it a challenge on a short week. The Raiders were awful against the Pats, but they will play better on offense here. They just won't stop the Bills. Pick: Bills 35, Raiders 21 Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers (-1.5) Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Packers blew out the Bears Sunday as Jordan Love lit up the skies. Look for more of that in this one against a bad Dallas secondary. The Cowboys struggled on defense against the Bucs, and that will continue in this one. Love continues to play well. Packers win a shootout. Pick: Packers 31, Cowboys 27 Washington Commanders at San Francisco 49ers (-7.5) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is a long road trip for the Commanders off a brutal tie last week to face the league's best team right now. That's a tough combination. They can only hope for a letdown by the 49ers after they beat Seattle last week. It won't happen. The 49ers continue to roll as Brock Purdy continues to make a claim as a legitimate MVP candidate. picks.blurb: Steelers vs. Buccaneers Week 6 Tracker: Injury updates, predictions, storylines and more - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers take 3-0 NLCS lead WNBA All-Defensive first team Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Caleb's return won't solve it all Pittsburgh Steelers RB Jaylen Warren (L) and Tampa Bay Buccaneers edge rusher Rueben Bain Jr. (R) | Lauren Leigh Bacho and Perry Knotts - Getty Images | Graphic by Adam Patrick Shayne Kubas Wed, October 14, 2026 at 10:00 AM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Coming off their thrilling 34-22 home victory over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 5, the 3-2 Pittsburgh Steelers head south this week to face the 1-4 Tampa Bay Buccaneers, who themselves are coming off their first win of the season last week against the Dallas Cowboys. Despite their record (and an injury to starting quarterback Baker Mayfield), the Bucs are coming off their two most competitive games of the season, with undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels filling in for Mayfield. It looks as though Daniels will once again be the one under center against Pittsburgh, and they can't allow him to look nearly as comfortable as Dallas did a week ago. Tampa Bay and Pittsburgh haven't played each other many times, but the Steelers have dominated those meetings 10-2. To keep pace in a hotly contested AFC North, they badly need that to become 11-2 this weekend. Everything you could want to know about this matchup, including injury updates, weather forecasts, storylines, and more, can be found right here. So make sure to bookmark this page and come back throughout the week. How to Watch Pittsburgh Steelers vs Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 6 Date: Sunday, October 18 Time: 1:00 p.m. EST TV Network: CBS Announcers: Andrew Catalon (Play-by-Play), Logan Ryan (Color Analyst), AJ Ross (Sideline Reporter) Pittsburgh Steelers Injury Report for Week 6 Steelers injury reports will be available here once they are released, beginning Wednesday, October 14 Tampa Bay Buccaneers Injury Report for Week 6 Buccaneers injury reports will be available here once they are released, beginning Wednesday, October 14 Weather Forecast for Pittsburgh Steelers vs Tampa Buccaneers Week 6 Current Forecast ( via NFLWeather.com ) Temperature: 79 degrees Wind Speed: 20 mph Precipitation: Isolated Rain Showers Biggest Pittsburgh Steelers Storylines heading into Week 6 Can Jaylen Warren keep up his unbelievable run against a tough Tampa run defense? Calling what Jaylen Warren has done over the past three games "unbelievable may not be the right word, since many Steelers fans have seen glimpses of the level of play he's reached this season. Still, three consecutive games with over 125 yards from scrimmage is no small feat. In fact, Warren is the only player to do that so far this season. The Buccaneers will be his toughest test so far by a mile; however, they are allowing just 3.28 yards per attempt on the ground, according to Sumer Sports . If Warren can maintain his level of production against a tough opponent like Tampa Bay, then his breakout will feel even more real than it already does. Can the Steelers' run defense shut down another high-powered run game? No Derrick Harmon, no problem for the Steelers in Week 5 against the Colts' rushing attack. Despite facing star running back Jonathan Taylor, Pittsburgh completely shut down the run against Indianapolis. They allowed just 66 yards on 24 attempts for a measly 2.8 yards per carry. While Harmon's absence didn't hurt them last week, the Buccaneers' run game has actually been more efficient than the Colts' this year, even before the Steelers crushed them a week ago. Bucky Irving looks much more like the player who burst onto the scene as a rookie in 2024, increasing his yards-per-attempt average from 3.4 last season to 5.3 so far this year. If Pittsburgh can slow him down with Harmon still on Injured Reserve, it should give the unit a ton of confidence moving forward. Will Tampa Bay play more man coverage, and can the Steelers handle it if they do? The Steelers' offense looks much better over the past three games after struggling mightily to start the season, but their kryptonite has remained the same for most of their five games: man coverage. Pittsburgh's receivers simply aren't winning often enough when teams man them up, and Aaron Rodgers' unwillingness to stay calm in the pocket isn't exactly helping either. The old gunslinger can still carve up zone for the most part, but unless his receivers can win almost immediately against man, he simply doesn't have the same playmaking ability he once had. Tampa Bay has played man on just 19.1% of their snaps this season, according to Sumer Sports. Will that change against Pittsburgh? And if it does, can they find success despite being down three receivers? Speaking of... Will the Steelers' offense change at all with multiple receivers now on the shelf? Pittsburgh will head into Week 6 down three receivers : Roman Wilson, Michael Pittman Jr., and special teams ace Ben Skowronek. For a team that wants to live in 11 personnel and in the shotgun, it could mean a serious change in how they operate until at least one of them returns. Pittsburgh shifted to more 12 and 22 personnel in the second half of Week 5 once Wilson and Skowronek went down, but will that plan carry over into next week? It's hard to say for sure given how Rodgers and head coach Mike McCarthy prefer to run the offense, but I certainly hope they are smart enough to lean on their tight ends and running backs without their full group of playmakers available. Even when everyone has been healthy, they have been far more effective when using heavier formations, so the offense may actually be in a better situation despite the unfortunate injuries.
