Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Will Walsh Thu, October 15, 2026 at 5:44 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Week 6 is set to be rolling into living rooms all throughout the nation and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers are no longer winless. Todd Bowles and his pewter pirates managed to pull out a sensationally shocking upset of the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday Night Football. Behind the mighty galloping of Bucky Irving and the poise of UDFA Jalen Daniels, Tampa's marauders took over AT&T Stadium. This Sunday (for the third week in a row), it'll be another classic blueblood NFL franchise on the schedule for the Buccaneers— The Pittsburgh Steelers. "The offense can't score if they don't have the ball." How can the Buccaneers win? ARLINGTON, TX - OCTOBER 08: Bucky Irving #7 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers runs the ball during an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on October 8, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Bucs need to make sure they stay on schedule and stick to their gameplan. There are NFL teams that have the benefit of being able to get into different types of games and win in a variety of ways— The Buccaneers are not that team. If a win is in the cards, they need to make sure they are playing the hand that best suits them. Last week, in Dallas, Tampa did a phenomenal job of staying in the realm of football that they themselves are comfortable playing. The Buccaneers kept the ball on the ground, dominated time of possession— Starting with a 10-minute opening drive, and kept Dallas off-kilter. That dictation was not only an advantage for Tampa Bay, it's the reason they won. That in turn made the Cowboys play the game the Buccaneers needed to play, not the one Dallas wanted to play. It would be easy to say, 'If Bucky Irving rushes for nearly 200 yards, the Buccaneers have a good chance of winning' , but it's more than the yards on the stat sheet. Irving's performance was eye-popping, but it was the offense's ability to stay on the field that won Tampa Bay the game. The Buccaneers finished the game with just shy of 40 minutes time of possession, while Dallas' heralded offense held the ball for just 20. That discrepancy is catastrophic for any team to be on the wrong side of— Personified through the consistent cutaways by Amazon's broadcast as they kept showing defeated, disengaged, and dispirited Dallas Cowboys on the sideline. Consecutive weeks with 40 minutes of possession may not be on the docket, however, will the Buccaneers' offense be able to keep themselves steady, avoid turnovers, and push Pittsburgh to play the type of game Tampa wants to play? "The question isn't who is going to let me; it's who is going to stop me." How can the Buccaneers lose? The Steelers have had some inconsistent offense this year, but they've had 24-plus points in each of the last three weeks (30, 24, 34). Of course, they can't score if they don't play (See the above portion of this article). The Buccaneers' second best option for keeping Pittsburgh's points down, besides pilfering clock, is turnovers. Tampa's turnover differential on the season is not glamourous (-2). Maybe even more absurd, that hideous -2 sits boldly after the Bucs just had a +3 in their last contest. Aside from points themselves, nothing has ever been, or will ever be, a more clear determinant of wins and losses than turnovers. Teams that take the ball away win a lot more than teams that lose the ball. Having the ball means having more chances to score, more chances to score means more better odds you will score; ergo, turnovers are good. More importantly, for a struggling, very one-dimensional team like the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, turnovers level the playing field. The scenario is two-fold. Not only does it fall on your defense to force them, but your offense must avoid turnovers like a coach on the hot seat must avoid losing. Last week, Tampa hit the trifecta— Their defense (and special teams) took the ball away from Dallas three times. Jalen Daniels and the Bucs' offense did not turn the ball over at all and their coach on the heat seat avoided a loss. This week, it's not Dak Prescott it's Aaron Rodgers. Aaron Rodgers is a historically anti-turnover prone quarterback. The former Packers' legend, Jets' bust, and current Steelers' stopgap, has quite literally the greatest touchdown to interception ratio in NFL history— As in, number one. Rodgers is not the type of quarterback that you want to face if the gameplan is get the ball— however , against all odds, Tampa Bay's ever assailed head coach Todd Bowles has actually had a healthy level of success against Rodgers during his Bucs' tenure. The two haven't matched up since Rodgers left Green Bay, but the duels have actually largely favored Bowles. In three games versus Todd Bowles' Tampa Bay defense, Rodgers has a losing record and has looked extremely ordinary. The four-time NFL MVP has wracked up just five touchdowns and he's also tossed four interceptions. The backdrop is laid out much differently for the 2026 edition, Rodgers has a new team, a new (his old) coach, is playing at a completely different level (which may actually further favor Bowles), and Bowles does not have nearly the same defensive firepower he once did. Sunday, will likely be the last time the two battle— A final chapter in the story. The storylines for Sunday's Bowles-Rodgers epilogue, can Todd Bowles get him again? Rodgers has yet to play a clean game against Bowles' Bucs. Will the Buccaneers' offense be able to stay mistake free for a second straight week? Turnovers, like they had against Rodgers' former team two weeks ago, will almost assuredly sink them into a self-dug 1-5 hole.

The Pittsburgh Steelers are currently 2.5-point favorites for their Week 6 road game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. However, NFL analyst Conor Orr thinks the oddsmakers have it completely wrong. Orr predicts the Steelers will continue their hot streak and dominate the Buccaneers in Week 6. "I wanna see the Steelers go down to Tampa Bay and win another one of these games," Orr said . "I think they can win this game by three touchdowns." Orr has done a complete 180 in just a matter of a week. Heading into Week 5, he begged the Indianapolis Colts to put the Steelers out of their misery. "Clearly you have communication issues. Your coach came out and said your house is dirty and you need to clean your house. Something's a mess here," Orr said on the Heed the Call NFL Podcast . "I'm sick of [Aaron Rodgers]. I'm sick of watching this team. I'm sick of the receivers dropping balls. I'm sick of them having played one good game against the Bengals so we've got to take them seriously for another three weeks. Come on, Jonathan Taylor. Put up 400 yards and put his old, dying horse out of its misery and off my screen." However, after watching the Steelers offense come alive in their latest win, Orr issued an apology to the team and now seems to be a big believer in Pittsburgh. "I have totally done a 180, and I'll admit it, on this Steelers offense," Orr continued. "Down so many people, and even down to Ben Skowronek, this team has been able to find a way to manufacture points. Aaron Rodgers will have bad Rodgers games, but I've totally flipped on this." The Steelers do seem to have some new found life. Rodgers is playing very well and running back Jaylen Warren has been on another level, recording 176, 126 and 188-yard performances the past three weeks. The only question that remains is: Can the Steelers offense continue this type of production the rest of the season? Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Dowdle Closing in on Return After missing three games in a row, Dowdle is finally on the precipice of a return for Pittsburgh. While speaking with reporters last week, the 28-year-old laid out how the entire process played out in that contest. "The first time I did it, I came to the sideline and I was like, "I think my toe broke,'" Dowdle said. "So I went to the tent and it was dislocated and they popped it back in, did the X-rays. Nothing was broken or whatever, but once they popped it back in, I felt good, so I'm like, 'I wanna go back in the game and play.' Dr. [James] Bradley was like, 'No, we're playing on turf, think I'm gonna be done,' because when you get it, you hurt the plate at the bottom or whatever. So I ended up talking him into going back in, and he was like, 'If it pop out again, you've gotta be done,' and it popped out again, so I had to be done." Benton was a surprise inclusion on the first injury report this week , though it doesn't appear that he's dealing with a serious ankle injury considering he's been upgraded to a limited participant alongside Ramsey. The game designations for both players remains to be seen when the final injury report is put out on October 16, but it certainly would appear they'll each be active against the Bucs. Steelers Get Good Injury News Before Bucs Game Skip to main content SI.COM The Pittsburgh Steelers have some positive developments on the injury front ahead of their Week 6 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . On their penultimate injury report of the week, running back Rico Dowdle (toe) was listed as a full participant, which is the first time that's been the case since he suffered his injury in Week 2 vs. the New England Patriots. He dislocated his toe twice against the Patriots, first in the second quarter and then in the third quarter in what was a 20-3 loss for the Steelers. Following the team's Week 5 victory over the Indianapolis Colts, head coach Mike McCarthy stated that Dowdle was close to playing in that game . Now, all the stars are aligning for him to be back on the field against the Bucs, even if it's not 100 percent official that he'll be active just yet. Jaylen Warren will remain the feature back given that he has posted 491 yards in the three contests Dowdle has missed, but the latter will certainly still have a noticeable role in the offense. Aller/Getty Images) Getty Mike Asti Thu, October 15, 2026 at 10:21 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads After Wednesday's news created concern that the Pittsburgh Steelers would be without another defensive lineman, more recent news provides optimism about Keeanu Benton playing this weekend. Keeanu Benton Could Be on Track to Play on Sunday Filling in admirably for second-year defensive tackle Derrick Harmon, who's dealing with a left foot injury and is on injured reserve for at least another three weeks, Benton has 12 combined tackles, with half credited as solo and the other half assisted, two quarterback hits and one pass deflection through Pittsburgh's first five games of the season. He had three tackles and that pass deflection in the Steelers' 34-22 win over the Indianapolis Colts. Benton is Part of the Future of the Steelers' Defensive Line At 25, Benton is a player the Steelers are planning to rely even more on in the future, especially with what can be expected from veteran defensive captain Cam Heyward dwindling as he continues to age. The Steelers selected Benton with the 49th overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft, bringing him to Pittsburgh after stellar college career in the Big Ten. Benton was named a second-team All-Big Ten player in 2021 and a member of the third-team for his senior season in 2022. He made 81 total tackles with nine sacks, four pass deflections, two forced fumbles, two fumble recoveries and a defensive touchdown in 39 games at the University of Wisconsin . away.headline: Report: Steelers WR Roman Wilson (finger) to miss multiple weeks
away.blurb: Wilson had no catches on one target before exiting in the second quarter of the 34-22 win. He was grabbing his left hand after an incompletion and did not return to the game. ESPN reported that Wilson is still gathering more information about the injury and will seek a second opinion. Wilson, a third-round pick in the 2024 NFL Draft by Pittsburgh, has 14 receptions for 188 yards and two touchdowns in five games this season. The 25-year-old has 26 receptions for 354 yards and four TDs over the last two seasons for the Steelers. Wilson’s status comes after Pittsburgh placed wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) on injured reserve Saturday and Ben Skowronek also left Sunday’s game with a calf injury. By Jordan Sigler 0 Share Newsweek is a Trust Project member See more of our trusted coverage when you search. Prefer Newsweek on Google to see more of our trusted coverage when you search. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are looking for their second win of the season when they host the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 6 on Sunday. The Buccaneers started the season 0-4, but pulled off a 24-16 upset of the Dallas Cowboys in Week 5 thanks to a strong running game by Bucky Irving, who rushed for 165 yards and a score on 21 carries. The win was the first of backup quarterback Jalon Daniels' career. It appears the Buccaneers will be counting on Daniels to get his second win on Sunday. More news: Exclusive: Breakout NFL Executives Who Could Become Future General Managers More news: 4 QBs Generating Serious Trade Buzz Weeks Before NFL Regular Season Starts Per multiple reports, Daniels is set to start against the Steelers as Baker Mayfield was not back to practice on Thursday. Mayfield suffered a dislocated thumb on his right (throwing) hand in the Buccaneers' 23-17 loss to the Minnesota Vikings in Week 3. On Wednesday, Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said Mayfield is getting better, but Tampa Bay does not want to start him if he's not playing at 100% on game day, and that could mean he doesn't get the start against the Carolina Panthers in Week 7. "Not at this time. Nothing has changed," Bowles said of Mayfield's status, via The Tampa Bay Times. "I mean, he's getting better. We'll see how much he throws and how he looks... I can't answer that until he throws the ball, where he's at. If he's not 100%, he doesn't need to play." Through three games, Daniels has thrown for 337 yards, two touchdowns, and three interceptions. He's played well, but Tampa Bay needs its franchise quarterback back as soon as possible to make a push in the NFC South. For more on the Buccaneers and the NFL , head to Newsweek Sports .

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are looking for their second win of the season when they host the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 6 on Sunday. The Buccaneers started the season 0-4, but pulled off a 24-16 upset of the Dallas Cowboys in Week 5 thanks to a strong running game by Bucky Irving, who rushed for 165 yards and a score on 21 carries. The win was the first of backup quarterback Jalon Daniels' career. It appears the Buccaneers will be counting on Daniels to get his second win on Sunday. More news: Exclusive: Breakout NFL Executives Who Could Become Future General Managers More news: 4 QBs Generating Serious Trade Buzz Weeks Before NFL Regular Season Starts Per multiple reports, Daniels is set to start against the Steelers as Baker Mayfield was not back to practice on Thursday. Mayfield suffered a dislocated thumb on his right (throwing) hand in the Buccaneers' 23-17 loss to the Minnesota Vikings in Week 3. On Wednesday, Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said Mayfield is getting better, but Tampa Bay does not want to start him if he's not playing at 100% on game day, and that could mean he doesn't get the start against the Carolina Panthers in Week 7. "Not at this time. Nothing has changed," Bowles said of Mayfield's status, via The Tampa Bay Times. "I mean, he's getting better. We'll see how much he throws and how he looks... I can't answer that until he throws the ball, where he's at. If he's not 100%, he doesn't need to play." Through three games, Daniels has thrown for 337 yards, two touchdowns, and three interceptions. He's played well, but Tampa Bay needs its franchise quarterback back as soon as possible to make a push in the NFC South. For more on the Buccaneers and the NFL , head to Newsweek Sports .

Los Angeles enters the game at 2-3 after a heartbreaking 37-34 overtime loss to the Buffalo Bills on Monday night. Arizona is 1-4 and coming off a disappointing 45-21 defeat against the Detroit Lions. Both teams need a strong performance, making Sunday's divisional matchup an important opportunity to build momentum. Kickoff is scheduled for 4:05 p.m. ET on FOX at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California. Matthew Stafford Leads the Rams Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford will be a major factor in Sunday's game as Los Angeles looks to rebound from its difficult loss to Buffalo. Stafford has thrown for 1,572 yards and nine touchdowns through five games, establishing himself as the centerpiece of an offense capable of producing explosive plays. However, six interceptions have created problems, and protecting the football will be important against Arizona. Head coach Sean McVay will look to get the offense back on track by utilizing his talented group of playmakers. Wide receivers Puka Nacua and Davante Adams give Stafford two dangerous options in the passing game, while running back Kyren Williams provides balance on the ground. Williams has recorded 343 rushing yards and four rushing touchdowns, making him an important part of Los Angeles' offensive attack. The Rams will also need to adjust along the offensive line, with left tackle Alaric Jackson suspended for Sunday's matchup. Jacoby Brissett Looks to Keep Arizona Competitive Arizona quarterback Jacoby Brissett will lead the Cardinals as they attempt to bounce back from their loss to Detroit. Brissett has thrown for 1,110 yards and nine touchdowns this season. Despite Arizona's struggles, he has shown the ability to move the football through the air and keep the offense competitive. Tight end Trey McBride remains one of his most reliable targets, entering the matchup with 42 receptions for 308 yards and three touchdowns. Rookie running back Jeremiyah Love has also contributed to Arizona's offense, although his availability and workload will be worth monitoring after he missed practice Wednesday with an ankle issue. First-year head coach Mike LaFleur will need his offense to produce consistently against a Rams defense looking to force turnovers and create pressure. A Crucial NFC West Matchup Sunday's game gives Los Angeles an opportunity to recover from its overtime defeat and improve its record. Arizona needs a stronger defensive performance after allowing 45 points against Detroit. With Stafford leading an explosive passing attack and Brissett looking to keep the Cardinals competitive, both quarterbacks will face important challenges. Recovered from the right high-ankle sprain suffered in the Aug. 13 preseason game against the Las Vegas Raiders , his left ankle has been an issue for several weeks. He has felt good heading into games, but then aggravation occurs on the field. Head coach Mike LaFleur said, “Want to get this ankle right and do it the right way. He’s a tough dude. You guys see the way he plays and how aggressive he is with his cuts. Imagine being a running back in the NFL, trying to put the foot down and cut the way that you’re capable of. We all are in agreeance, as much as he wants to battle through, we’re all in agreeance right now that (he needs to) give a little bit of rest and see as the week goes on what that’ll entail for Sunday.” Asked about concern about it continuing to be a problem going forward, LaFleur said, “It’s an ankle, so you don’t know. I’m not a doctor and each body is a little bit different. The way he came back from the one in the preseason was unbelievable. He also has the potential to develop at the NFL level like any player does. If Trost sees game action this year, then he'll be doing both: Getting experience now, and developing for the future. As long as he can stay healthy. At this point, if a player is suiting up for the Rams, they have the potential to play. McVay said after the latest loss to the Buffalo Bills that all options were on the table. If Trost can stay healthy, he'll be one of those options for the Rams. Perhaps he'll be an option to bolster the blocking on their field goal unit.

home.headline: Jeremiyah Love Gets Concerning Injury Update Ahead of Cardinals-Rams
home.blurb: TEMPE — The Arizona Cardinals are holding star rookie running back Jeremiyah Love out of practice on Wednesday as Week 6 preperations for the Los Angeles Rams ramp up. Jeremiyah Love Gets Concerning Injury Update Ahead of Cardinals-Rams Skip to main content SI.COM "Take him one day at a time. You know, we want to get this ankle right and do it the right way," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters on Wednesday. Love has been nursing an ankle injury through the opening stages of his rookie season after suffering a different ankle injury during preseason. While he hasn't missed any regular season action, Love's participation and impact has been slightly hindered. There's been some talks about potentially shutting Love down to allow the ankle to heal, though LaFleur didn't seem willing to do that. Arizona is just 1-4 and is again favored to lose in Los Angeles. "Listen, I'm going to try to be as candid as possible with also knowing that everyone's listening to this too, right? But he's a tough dude. You guys see the way he plays and how aggressive he is with his cuts. I mean, imagine being a running back in the NFL trying to put the foot down and cut the way that you know that you're capable of," LaFleur said. "And so we all are in agreeance — as much as you know he wants to battle through — we're all in agreeance right now, it's just hey, give [the injury] a little bit of rest and see as the week goes on, what that'll entail for Sunday." Love, the No. 3 overall pick, has 67 carries for 245 yards and one touchdown on the ground while adding 11 receptions for 36 yards and a score through the air. "I think early at his career [he battled injuries], but you had the right [ankle] early, and then now you got the left one. So now you're just kind of — it's just double dipping. The right side, the preseason one's fine. It's the other one right now that's the lingering issue. They're ankles, you know, it's an ankle. I'm not a doctor, and each body's a little bit different," LaFleur continued. "Like the way he came back from the one in the preseason was unbelievable, like he doesn't even feel it. But this one is the one that happened kind of when the regular season started, and it just lingered." Has Love lost any of his explosiveness? "You'd have to ask him that," LaFleur added. "I know how explosive he is. I know how explosive he wants to be. So I mean I think that's a fair assessment in some aspects. Again, I don't think it's an overall hindrance, but again the the rest for him is going to be vital." picks.blurb: Chiefs-Chargers betting line & game prediction: KC faces desperate AFC West rival - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers take 3-0 NLCS lead WNBA All-Defensive first team Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Caleb's return won't solve it all Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III (9) dives to the pylon to complete a 22-yard touchdown scamper against the Las Vegas Raiders during a Week 4 NFL game at Allegiant Stadium in Paradise, Nevada, on Sunday, Oct. 4, 2026. (David Brytus/IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) Pete Sweeney Thu, October 15, 2026 at 12:30 PM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Kansas City Chiefs return from their bye week hoping to build on their perfect 4-0 record as they welcome a Los Angeles Chargers team that has lost five straight to start the season. Sunday's game marks the second straight AFC West matchup for the Chiefs and Chargers. Kansas City defeated the Las Vegas Raiders 30-27 on the road in Week 4, and this past Sunday, Los Angeles lost 23-17 to the Denver Broncos. How to watch Chargers at Chiefs Kickoff: 3:25 p.m. Central Time Where: Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City TV: CBS (Channel 5 in Kansas City) Radio: KFNZ (96.5 FM in Kansas City, KNSS 98.7 FM in Wichita) Betting line: Chiefs -8.5 Behind the LAC-KC matchup The last time the Chargers visited Arrowhead Stadium, it was one of the grimmest days in a decade for the dynastic Chiefs. In a game in which Kansas City needed a win to keep its playoff hopes alive, Patrick Mahomes tore his ACL and LCL , with Los Angeles eventually winning 16-13. The Chargers beat the Dallas Cowboys the following week but dropped two games to close the season, missing the playoffs. The December victory against Dallas still stands as their last win here in mid-October. As expected, Chiefs head coach Andy Reid is not looking too much into their winless start. "Good football team — we know that," Reid said. "Records don't matter. They've been in every game, and they're playing their tail off. So we're going to get ready for a tough AFC West battle there. Jim (Harbaugh) does a heck of a job with that crew." To Reid's point — and it's been a rather familiar one in Kansas City — the Chargers have lost each of their last three games by one score. Reid would later note Los Angeles' long injury list, which will have an impact on both sides of the ball. Because of several injuries to their offensive line, including those to star tackles Rashawn Slater (ankle) and Joe Alt (neck), the Chargers used a rookie-heavy group against Denver, with Herbert taking five sacks. Slater is currently on injured reserve, and Alt did not practice Wednesday. Through five games, Herbert has taken 17 total sacks — the second-highest mark in the league. The stat could play well for the Chiefs, who are looking for their first sack since recording four in their opening-night win against the Broncos. "There's a lot of things that go into it," defensive end George Karlaftis said. "From protection and quarterback getting rid of the ball and all that kind of stuff. Ultimately, for us as a front seven, defensive line, we've got to get the quarterback on the ground by any means necessary, and we've got to do a better job of that." Los Angeles' woes aren't exclusive to the offensive line. In addition to Alt, the Chargers listed 19 more players on their Wednesday injury report. Left guard Kayode Awosika (fibula), wide receiver Tre Harris (hamstring), cornerback Donte Jackson (hamstring) and safety Derwin James (hamstring) were among those held out because of injury. James has missed the last two games, and if he misses a third, it could spell trouble against tight end Travis Kelce. Now in his 14th season, Kelce has had his share of battles with James, and he comes into the game leading the Chiefs with 246 receiving yards. Kelce's involvement will be even more important with Tyquan Thornton heading to injured reserve and Rashee Rice missing the first practice of the week because of his hamstring injury. The injuries to Thornton and Rice should mean additional opportunities for Jalen Royals, Cyrus Allen and the recently reacquired Justin Watson, who may be elevated from the practice squad. "They've put in the work," quarterback Patrick Mahomes said. "We've had the guys in front of them with Tyquan going out there and playing great football, and so they've had to put in the work at practice. And they've been doing that and doing that. And so now their number gets called, and they're gonna step into the role and do their job. And so I'm excited for them." Of course, the Chiefs' 2026 offensive plan begins with running back Kenneth Walker, who will look to pick up right where he left off following his extraordinary start . Entering Week 6, Walker ranks among the league's top-five players with 621 yards from scrimmage, and Pro Football Focus credits him with a league-leading 39 missed tackles forced. Walker's seamless impact should help keep Mahomes upright, with the Los Angeles edge group of Khalil Mack, Akheem Mesidor and Tuli Tuipulotu having combined for 6.5 sacks. The presence of Walker has opened up play-action shots that are working well for the Chiefs. Although left tackle Josh Simmons (back) practiced on a limited basis Wednesday , Reid said the Chiefs plan to ease him back in, which means his highly anticipated return may have to wait until next week at the earliest. The Chargers hired offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel this offseason with hopes of getting the most out of Herbert, but offensive-line injuries and other struggles have contributed to a difficult start for the quarterback, who has thrown seven interceptions and posted a 70.2 passer rating. Herbert has often responded to the pocket collapsing by using his legs, as he's rushed for 142 yards on 24 attempts, or 5.9 yards a carry. Defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo will be tasked with pushing Herbert toward what Harbaugh has called "desperation time," where Herbert has tried to carry the entire offense himself. That could mean a Chiefs-friendly script that presents Kansas City's healthy secondary with turnover opportunities. With all the injuries to the passing offense, Los Angeles may need to muck up the game and rely heavily on its three-headed rushing attack of Omarion Hampton, Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal. No matter how they make it happen, the Chargers will have to find a way to win or risk entering their Week 8 bye without a victory. Chargers-Chiefs game prediction If not for the Chargers' outrageous injury list, this would make for the perfect situation to pick a surprise Los Angeles win, or at the very least a cover. But when you examine everything — the Chiefs' hot start, the reinvigorated offense led by Walker and Reid's impressive career record coming off a bye — it all seems like too much. The Chargers initially make it interesting before the Chiefs settle in and continue doing what they have done all season. Kansas City is 4-0 after its bye, while Los Angeles is 0-5 following a 23-17 loss to Denver. Kickoff at Arrowhead Stadium is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET. The Chiefs are favored by 8.5 points, but a routine favorite winning comfortably would hardly qualify as a bold prediction. Instead, this forecast projects an exceptional rushing performance, an unexpected Chargers defensive highlight and a fourth-quarter rally that changes the complexion of the afternoon without changing the winner. Kenneth Walker III rushes for 200 yards and three touchdowns Jay Biggerstaff-Imagn Images Walker has already accumulated 537 rushing yards and four touchdowns on 87 carries through four games. That translates to more than six yards per attempt, giving Kansas City a foundation for dominating without asking Patrick Mahomes to carry every possession. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Chiefs average 6.5 yards per offensive play compared with the Chargers' 4.8. Their third-down conversion rate is also substantially better: 44% against 34.85%. Those advantages can sustain drives and produce the repeated rushing opportunities necessary for a monster individual afternoon. The prediction goes beyond another efficient outing. Walker reaches 200 rushing yards for the game and scores three times, becoming the central reason Kansas City controls possession and repeatedly finishes drives. There is an important limitation: Los Angeles allows only 5.0 yards per play, the same figure as Kansas City. This is not a forecast built on pretending the Chargers cannot defend. It depends on Walker maintaining his explosiveness while the Chiefs create an unusually favorable game script. If Kansas City builds an early advantage, sustained rushing volume can turn Walker's strong start into the biggest performance of his season. The Chargers intercept Patrick Mahomes twice, including a pick-six Mahomes has thrown nine touchdown passes against two interceptions through four games, with a 106.2 passer rating. Predicting two interceptions in one afternoon means Los Angeles matches his entire season total, despite entering winless. The statistical route to that surprise exists. The Chargers allow opponents to convert just 31.25% of third downs, compared with Kansas City's 37.04%. Forcing longer, obvious passing situations could provide opportunities that disappear when Walker keeps the offense ahead of schedule. Los Angeles needs more than ordinary defensive stops because its offense averages just 16.8 points per game. A defensive touchdown would change both field position and scoreboard pressure without requiring Justin Herbert to repeatedly rescue stalled possessions. The call is that one aggressive coverage read becomes an interception return for a touchdown, while another takeaway interrupts a promising Chiefs drive. That would be an unexpected blemish on Mahomes' efficient opening month. It would also illustrate why a team's record does not eliminate its capacity to produce a game-changing individual moment. Justin Herbert leads a 17-point fourth quarter, but Kansas City survives Herbert's current numbers make this the most counterintuitive offensive prediction: 937 passing yards, five touchdowns, seven interceptions and a 70.2 passer rating through five games. He has also absorbed 17 sacks. Against Denver, he managed 121 passing yards and was sacked five times. Receiving availability remains uncertain after Ladd McConkey dressed without playing, Quentin Johnston missed the game and Tre' Harris suffered a hamstring injury. Nevertheless, the prediction is that Herbert finally finds rhythm against a defense protecting a substantial lead. Two touchdown drives and a field goal produce 17 fourth-quarter points, forcing Kansas City to finish the game with its offense rather than coast. Walker provides that answer. away.headline: Chiefs first-round DT Peter Woods pops up on injury report days before Chargers game
away.blurb: Following Thursday's practice, that became even more obvious. In addition to left tackle Josh Simmons and cornerback L'Jarius Sneed being limited and wideout Rashee Rice not participating, another standout player was added to the list. Woods, the No. 29 overall selection out of Clemson, has played 126 defensive snaps thus far, good for 46% of those available. He hasn't made a sizable impact in the box score, amassing nine tackles and a pass deflection. With that said, the athletic interior lineman is credited with one pressure and three "stops" by Pro Football Focus . Tracking is a bit different on NFL Pro , which gives him seven stops in four games. Simmons continuing to be a limited participant shouldn't surprise anyone. The 2025 first-rounder is coming off a significant back injury and is clearly being eased back into the fold following over a half-dozen weeks off. Sneed being limited with knee management is a non-story. Three Ways Josh Simmons' Eventual Return Can Help Chiefs Moving Forward With each passing second, the Kansas City Chiefs are getting closer and closer to their Week 6 showdown at home versus the Los Angeles Chargers. Head coach Andy Reid's crew is hard at work preparing for a bitter division rival to come to down, but the club's injury situation is less than ideal. Per the team on Thursday afternoon, rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods appeared on an updated version of the injury report. The first-round pick is now nursing a neck ailment after not being listed at all on Wednesday when the club had three players (safety Chamarri Conner, fullback Ben VanSumeren and quarterback Patrick Mahomes) deemed full participants. The silver lining here is there's no reason to worry about Woods just yet. According to Matt Derrick of Chiefs Digest , the neck issue is "not considered a big deal." Rice, who hurt his hamstring in Week 4's triumph over the Las Vegas Raiders, is a player to keep an eye on. Given that he hasn't gotten any work for consecutive days, it's becoming increasingly difficult to see him being active this weekend against Los Angeles. Reid typically prefers noteworthy participation in the final practice of the week, so there's still some hope, but Rice would have to be brought along quickly. Once Friday's practice is over with, the overarching takeaway could be whether Woods bounces back and receives a full workload. home.headline: Chiefs first-round DT Peter Woods pops up on injury report days before Chargers game
home.blurb: Following Thursday's practice, that became even more obvious. In addition to left tackle Josh Simmons and cornerback L'Jarius Sneed being limited and wideout Rashee Rice not participating, another standout player was added to the list. Woods, the No. 29 overall selection out of Clemson, has played 126 defensive snaps thus far, good for 46% of those available. He hasn't made a sizable impact in the box score, amassing nine tackles and a pass deflection. With that said, the athletic interior lineman is credited with one pressure and three "stops" by Pro Football Focus . Tracking is a bit different on NFL Pro , which gives him seven stops in four games. Simmons continuing to be a limited participant shouldn't surprise anyone. The 2025 first-rounder is coming off a significant back injury and is clearly being eased back into the fold following over a half-dozen weeks off. Sneed being limited with knee management is a non-story. Three Ways Josh Simmons' Eventual Return Can Help Chiefs Moving Forward With each passing second, the Kansas City Chiefs are getting closer and closer to their Week 6 showdown at home versus the Los Angeles Chargers. Head coach Andy Reid's crew is hard at work preparing for a bitter division rival to come to down, but the club's injury situation is less than ideal. Per the team on Thursday afternoon, rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods appeared on an updated version of the injury report. The first-round pick is now nursing a neck ailment after not being listed at all on Wednesday when the club had three players (safety Chamarri Conner, fullback Ben VanSumeren and quarterback Patrick Mahomes) deemed full participants. The silver lining here is there's no reason to worry about Woods just yet. According to Matt Derrick of Chiefs Digest , the neck issue is "not considered a big deal." Rice, who hurt his hamstring in Week 4's triumph over the Las Vegas Raiders, is a player to keep an eye on. Given that he hasn't gotten any work for consecutive days, it's becoming increasingly difficult to see him being active this weekend against Los Angeles. Reid typically prefers noteworthy participation in the final practice of the week, so there's still some hope, but Rice would have to be brought along quickly. Once Friday's practice is over with, the overarching takeaway could be whether Woods bounces back and receives a full workload. home.headline: Former Super Bowl champion WR has status upgraded ahead of return game against Chiefs
home.blurb: KANSAS CITY, Mo. (KCTV) - A two-time Super Bowl champion with the Kansas City Chiefs is getting closer to his first return to Arrowhead Stadium since leaving the franchise. The 32-year-old wide receiver who won back-to-back Super Bowls with the Chiefs in 2022 and 2023 was upgraded from a limited participant in Wednesday’s practice to a full participant Thursday, the Chargers said. Valdes-Scantling is dealing with a rib injury. This season, he has 2 receptions for 22 yards in three games with the Chargers. He signed with Los Angeles’ practice squad in September after spending the preseason with the Dallas Cowboys and being released Aug. 30. Valdes-Scantling’s role in Los Angeles has increased in recent weeks as the Chargers have dealt with injuries to multiple wide receivers, including Ladd McConkey (foot), Quentin Johnston (chest) and Tre’ Harris (hamstring). Valdes-Scantling signed with the Chiefs as a free agent ahead of the 2022 season, leaving Green Bay to come to Kansas City. After leaving the Chiefs following the 2023 season, Valdes-Scantling has bounced around the league. He’s spent time on the active roster during the regular season in Buffalo, New Orleans, San Francisco, Pittsburgh and Los Angeles. During his time with the Chiefs, Valdes-Scantling had 63 receptions for 1,002 yards and 3 touchdowns in the regular season. In the playoffs, he had several key moments, including touchdowns in the 2022 AFC Championship Game and 2023 Super Bowl, as well as the game-sealing catch in the AFC Championship Game in Baltimore in 2023 as well. It will be the first time Valdes-Scantling has gone up against the Chiefs since leaving the organization.

home.headline: Chiefs’ WR injury woes could be fixed with one major trade
home.blurb: Knox recently named the Chiefs as a possible landing spot for disgruntled Cleveland Browns wide receiver Jerry Jeudy, suggesting the Chiefs could send the Browns a conditional 2027 fifth-round pick in return. “According to NFL insider Jordan Schultz, it’s ‘pretty well known around the league’ that Jeudy is available,” Knox wrote . “Per Schultz, the Browns would prefer to get a third- or fourth-round pick in exchange for the receiver, though that may be difficult. “The 27-year-old struggled through last season and has fallen out of the game plan this year as Concepcion, Boston, and tight end Harold Fannin Jr. have become the go-to targets. Still, Jeudy is a talented pass-catcher who made the Pro Bowl just two years ago following a 1,229-yard season. His skill set hasn’t disappeared, and his 2026 base salary of $1.5 million should appeal to budget-conscious teams.” The Kansas City Chiefs have been pretty snake-bitten when it comes to keeping healthy wide receivers on their roster. Second-leading receiver Tyquan Thornton suffered a gruesome ankle injury nearly two weeks ago against the Las Vegas Raiders that will likely sideline him the rest of the season. Rashee Rice could miss some time with hamstring and knee injuries, and both Jeff Caldwell and Jimmy Holiday have been on injured reserve since the end of August. As things sit now, Xavier Worthy (14 catches, 133 yards, one touchdown), Jalen Royals (three catches, 17 yards, one TD), Cyrus Allen and Nikko Remigio are the only healthy WRs on Kansas City’s roster — and the latter two haven’t recorded a catch this season, which is why Kristopher Knox of Bleacher Report thinks they should look to upgrade the position. Jeudy (eight catches for 81 yards in five games) has been almost a non-factor this season with the emergence of Boston and Concepcion. However, he had a 90-reception, 1,229-yard, four-TD season just two years ago. In Kansas City he would see much more than the three targets per game he’s currently getting in Cleveland. Jeudy would also give quarterback Patrick Mahomes the kind of reliable big-play target he’s been missing ever since the team traded away Tyreek Hill. The Houston Texans just got their first win. The Dallas Cowboys can't get out of their own way, and the Buffalo Bills are mauling everyone in their way. It's been a wacky start to the season, which has made our NFL picks and predictions for every game each week a bit more difficult than I expected. We're having to adjust our perceptions and expectations on the fly, and we're still in the mix as we head into what should be a fascinating Week 6. Zach Rotman came out of the bullpen for me last week and came through with a solid week. Many, many thanks to him for helping the cause, but I'm back in the saddle now. Let's hope I don't make this thing go any further off the rails, but let's dive right into this fun slate with our NFL picks for Week 6 as we make predictions both straight-up and against the spread for all 14 games on the slate this week. Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER. Toughest NFL Week 6 prediction to make Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Buffalo Bills at Las Vegas Raiders (+5.5) The Buffalo Bills have been rolling, including toppling the Rams in overtime in Los Angeles on Monday night. Stop me if you've heard this one before, but Buffalo has one of the NFL's best offenses behind Josh Allen and it doesn't seem like there's a defense in the league that's going to be able to stop this team from scoring 30 points - they're quite literally averaging 32.7 points per game after the first five games of the year. Meanwhile, the Raiders have certainly fallen back to earth a bit, losing two straight after their 3-0 start to the season. At the same time, the Bills defense is the same problem it's been for the past few years. It seems like Buffalo has to produce at this level offensively to win games because the defense is going to give it up. While the Raiders might not be a surprise contender, they still look like a quite competent football team behind Kirk Cousins and, while Buffalo will be able to score on their defense, they're still averaging 26.4 points per game on the year. I think Buffalo still has the offensive firepower against a middling defense to get the win in this game. But with it being in Vegas against a team that has a legitimate pulse, it's going to be another shootout and one that could likely be decided by a field goal once again. 5.5 points is a bit too many, so we'll take the Raiders against the spread and pray. Easiest NFL Week 6 pick on the board Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Los Angeles Chargers at Kansas City Chiefs (-8.5) This line could've been two touchdowns and I'm still taking the Kansas City Chiefs over the division rival Chargers. For starters, what has LA shown this season to make you believe they have a chance in Arrowhead in Week 6? No, seriously. There's been little evidence to think that this game will be close as the Chiefs have been absolutely rolling on both sides of the ball while Justin Herbert delivers the worst season of his career, the Chargers defense is middling at its best and the self-inflicted wounds in each game from LA multiply likes the heads of a hydra. If that weren't enough, Andy Reid is famously one of the most lethal head coaches when his team is coming off of the bye week. This isn't to say that the Chiefs are a perfect team as I maintain that they still need to find some more upgrades at wide receiver, especially after the gnarly Tyquan Thornton injury. While that may be true, though, they are a far better coached and more talented team than the winless Chargers and I wouldn't be surprised if this game was lopsided and out of hand early in favor of the home side. The pick that probably has you scratching your head Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Dallas Cowboys (+1.5) at Green Bay Packers Coming off of a home loss to undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels and the previously winless Buccaneers, naturally I'm taking the Dallas Cowboys to go on the road to Lambeau and beat the Packers as underdogs. What about this doesn't make sense to you? Yes, the optics look strange. However, this isn't about expecting the Cowboys hiring Mike Pettine to essentially help out new defensive coordinator Christian Parker drastically improving the defense, though it can't hurt. It's more about this being a likely shootout between these two teams because, despite what happened to Tyson Bagent and the Bears, I still don't trust Green Bay on that side of the ball. Furthermore, I also still don't trust the Packers run game, even against Dallas. Expect this game to go back and forth throughout the action, but I believe the Cowboys are going to have more offensive firepower and some adjustments on the side of the ball you can actually trust Dallas on to attack Green Bay throughout. They might not come up with many stops of their own, but they'll have enough to pull out the win. Plus, just from a narrative perspective, if ever there was a time for the Cowboys to keep their fans from abandoning ship, it's a game like this, and this franchise has been masterful at doing exactly that over the years. picks.blurb: Bills vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 6 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers take 3-0 NLCS lead WNBA All-Defensive first team Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Caleb's return won't solve it all Bills vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 6 Tim Crean, ClutchPoints Tue, October 13, 2026 at 8:44 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Buffalo Bills face off against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 6. This matchup between the 4-1 Bills and the 3-2 Raiders gets a prime spot in the late Sunday window as one of the best games of the week. These two original AFC franchises haven't played a game with meaningful stakes for both teams since the 1993 "Just Freeze Baby" Divisional Round game . Now, as both sides come into this game with winning records, let's make some bold Bills-Raiders predictions. Start your Raiders in fantasy football The Bills are their own worst enemy so far this season, as they love to gift their opponents chances to stay in the game. Whether it is shockingly cavalier Josh Allen interceptions, infuriating James Cook fumbles, or the fact that the defense (outside of Deone Walker and Gregory Rousseau) looks like it has no clue what it is doing right now, Buffalo loves keeping the other team in the game. Sunday will be no different, as fans should expect at least two turnovers from the Bills' offense and long stretches where the Raiders' O looks like the 2007 New England Patriots. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) That means big games from the Raiders' defense, Kirk Cousins, Brock Bowers, Ashton Jeanty, and maybe even the likes of Mike Washington Jr., Michael Mayer, and Tre Tucker. So, for all you fantasy football players out there, any Raiders on your roster should be a good play in Week 6 . Josh Allen delivers again Despite the mediocre (or worse) play at times from the Bills' offensive line, wide receivers, tight end, and running backs, and defensive back seven, the Bills are 4-1 and leading the AFC East thanks to one man: Brandon Beane. Just kidding! He's the reason the rest of the team is struggling so much. The real reason is Josh Allen. Through five weeks, Allen is still the betting favorite for NFL MVP this year. Yes, Brock Bowers is playing great, and Patrick Mahomes is back, but if you define MVP as the players whose absence would tank his team's chances the most, Allen has to be the answer. Monday night's dramatic OT win over the preseason Super Bowl favorite Los Angeles Rams came courtesy of 210 yards passing and a staggering 121 yards rushing from the Bills QB. Sure, he threw his obligatory head-scratching pick in the first half, but in the second, it was a one-man battle with 53 Rams players, and the singular man won. Against the Raiders, expect more of the same. Vegas has an improved defense this season and an incredible pass rusher in Maxx Crosby, but that only means Allen will be forced to take off even more as usual. And with his receivers getting minimal separation and Cook's suspect ball security, it will be all Allen, all the time in Week 6. Bills 31, Raiders 24 This won't be a cakewalk for the Bills by any means, as the Raiders are one of (if not) the most improved teams in the league. We know Cousins is a professional QB, the Raiders have some incredible young offensive weapons, and Klint Kubiak seems like a legit NFL head coach with an incredibly bright future. Allen doesn't have those last two things, as his skill position core is the exact same as last year, as long as D.J. Moore is out injured and his "new" head coach is just the same offensive coordinator who couldn't get it done the past three seasons, but with a more impressive title. Nevertheless, Allen should be able to will his Bills to victory over the Raiders in Week 6 just by sheer force of talent and will. As good as Las Vegas has looked at times this season, they are probably a year or two away from being legit contenders. That's why we'll take the Buffalo to win here, and to do so by slightly more than the -5.5-point spread suggests. picks.headline: Bills vs. Raiders Preview: Buffalo Looks to Keep Rolling Against Las Vegas
picks.blurb: Bills vs. Raiders Preview: Buffalo Looks to Keep Rolling Against Las Vegas - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers take 3-0 NLCS lead WNBA All-Defensive first team Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Caleb's return won't solve it all Bills vs. Raiders Preview: Buffalo Looks to Keep Rolling Against Las Vegas Photo by: Bob DeChiara Stephan Stroud Thu, October 15, 2026 at 8:31 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Buffalo Bills head to Las Vegas on Sunday for a Week 6 matchup against the Raiders, with both teams looking to strengthen their positions in the AFC playoff race. Buffalo enters the game at 4-1 after an exciting 37-34 overtime victory over the Los Angeles Rams on Monday night. The Raiders, meanwhile, are 3-2 after suffering a 45-17 loss to the New England Patriots. With the Bills carrying one of the league's most productive offenses and Las Vegas looking to bounce back, Sunday's matchup at Allegiant Stadium presents an important test for both teams. Kickoff is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. Eastern on CBS. Josh Allen Leads Buffalo's Explosive Offense Quarterback Josh Allen remains the centerpiece of Buffalo's offense. Through five games, Allen has thrown for 1,249 yards and seven touchdowns while adding eight rushing touchdowns. His ability to create plays with both his arm and legs makes him one of the most difficult quarterbacks to defend. Allen was particularly dangerous against the Rams, throwing for 342 yards and two touchdowns while rushing for 121 yards. His performance helped Buffalo survive a back-and-forth contest and improve to 4-1. Running back James Cook has also been productive, rushing for 532 yards through five games. His speed and ability to create explosive plays give the Bills another weapon that Las Vegas must account for. Head coach Joe Brady will look to keep the offense balanced while helping Allen avoid costly turnovers. Buffalo has committed nine giveaways over its last three games, making ball security an important focus heading into Sunday. Raiders Need a Strong Response Las Vegas will look to quarterback Kirk Cousins to help the offense recover from its disappointing performance against New England. Cousins has thrown for 1,269 yards and 12 touchdowns through five games, giving the Raiders a capable passing attack. Tight end Brock Bowers has been one of Cousins' primary targets, recording 312 receiving yards and three touchdowns. His ability to create mismatches could be especially important against a Buffalo defense that has struggled to contain opposing passing attacks. The Raiders will also rely on running back Ashton Jeanty , who has rushed for 291 yards this season. Establishing the ground game could help Las Vegas control possession and prevent Allen from spending too much time on the field. Head coach Klint Kubiak will need his team to improve its offensive line play and limit mistakes after the loss to New England. A Major Test for Both Teams Buffalo enters the matchup averaging 32.8 points per game, while Las Vegas has averaged 26.4. Both defenses have experienced difficulties, creating opportunities for the offenses to make an impact. The Bills will try to maintain their momentum after the overtime win, while the Raiders need a response at home to remain competitive in the AFC West. With Allen's dual threat ability, Cousins' passing production and two offenses looking to establish control, Sunday's matchup could be an important measuring stick for both teams as the NFL season continues.

picks.blurb: Opening lines: Spread: Bills -6.5 Moneyline: Bills -270; Raiders +220 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Raiders vs Bills expert picks Adam Kaufman: Bills 34, Raiders 23 Las Vegas just allowed New England to hang 45 points. Now Josh Allen gets a turn. That's not an especially comforting sequence for Raiders fans. The Bills' shortened week after an overtime win against the Rams is worth considering, but Allen and James Cook have too many ways to attack a defense that needs substantial improvement. The Raiders' quarterback plan needs monitoring after No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza's debut. Whoever starts will need help from Brock Bowers and a balanced offense to keep Buffalo from running away. I expect Las Vegas to show more fight at home. I also expect the Bills to score enough that a respectable Raiders offensive performance still won't be enough to win. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Bills 38, Raiders 24 The shine of a 3-0 start might be fading for the Silver and Black. After getting dismantled by the Patriots, the Raiders now face the unenviable task of taking on another high-powered attack. Josh Allen should be able to pick on an inexperienced secondary and also get plenty of mileage out of Buffalo's ground game. Las Vegas could find more success through the air against a Buffalo defense that has repeatedly subjected the team to shootouts, but the Raiders might not have enough ammunition to come out on top. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Bills 31, Raiders 23 The shine might be coming off the Raiders. In what has been an awful scheduling spot, Vegas suffered a close loss to the Chiefs, traveled across the country to get blown out by the Patriots and now return home to deal with the Bills, of all teams. Good luck. Buffalo has some defensive issues to work through and that will eventually hurt them down the road. It won't matter in Week 6. Josh Allen's team gets another win out west. away.blurb: Starting right tackle Spencer Brown left Monday night's 37-34 victory over the Los Angeles Rams because of a back injury and did not return, adding another starter to Buffalo's list of health concerns. NFL teams have to submit a report on practice participation on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday for a Sunday game. There are three levels of practice participation that can be designated: did not participate, limited participation and full participation. Bills athletic trainers tended to Brown on the field before he walked off under his own power. He appeared to grab at his back while walking toward the sideline and went directly into the blue medical tent. Brown later went to the locker room and did not return. Buffalo initially listed Brown as questionable before downgrading him to out during the fourth quarter. He was listed as questionable but did not play Monday. Oliver did not practice at all last week. Joshua Palmer was ruled out against the Rams after suffering a shoulder injury during Friday's practice. Palmer was not listed on Thursday's injury report before being limited Friday and sitting out Saturday. He was listed as questionable but was inactive against the Rams. Zane Durant is eligible to return after beginning the season on injured reserve. Buffalo can designate Durant to return and open his 21-day practice window when he is medically cleared. Tyrell Shavers is eligible to return after beginning the season on the physically unable to perform list. The Bills can designate him to return and open his 21-day practice window when he is ready. Ashton Jeanty played against New England despite being listed as questionable because of ankle and foot injuries. "Unless I can't run, jump, I'm playing. Football is a tough game. You're never gonna play feeling 100 percent," Jeanty said. "So at the end of the day, I just want to go out there and do my best for my teammates and whatever it takes." away.blurb: Rams Injury Report, Week 5 vs. Bills: Defensive end Aaron Donald, tight end Colby Parkinson and cornerback Jaylen Watson good to go for Monday Night Football; Quentin Lake questionable but 'trending in the right direction' Skip to main content Primary nav TEAM WOODLAND HILLS, Calif. – Rams defensive end Aaron Donald (back), tight end Colby Parkinson (knee/shoulder) and cornerback Jaylen Watson (shoulder) have no game status designations on the Week 5 Injury Report, clearing the way for them to return on Monday Night Football against the Bills at SoFi Stadium (5:15 p.m. PT, ESPN and ABC). home.blurb: Starting right tackle Spencer Brown left Monday night's 37-34 victory over the Los Angeles Rams because of a back injury and did not return, adding another starter to Buffalo's list of health concerns. NFL teams have to submit a report on practice participation on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday for a Sunday game. There are three levels of practice participation that can be designated: did not participate, limited participation and full participation. Bills athletic trainers tended to Brown on the field before he walked off under his own power. He appeared to grab at his back while walking toward the sideline and went directly into the blue medical tent. Brown later went to the locker room and did not return. Buffalo initially listed Brown as questionable before downgrading him to out during the fourth quarter. He was listed as questionable but did not play Monday. Oliver did not practice at all last week. Joshua Palmer was ruled out against the Rams after suffering a shoulder injury during Friday's practice. Palmer was not listed on Thursday's injury report before being limited Friday and sitting out Saturday. He was listed as questionable but was inactive against the Rams. Zane Durant is eligible to return after beginning the season on injured reserve. Buffalo can designate Durant to return and open his 21-day practice window when he is medically cleared. Tyrell Shavers is eligible to return after beginning the season on the physically unable to perform list. The Bills can designate him to return and open his 21-day practice window when he is ready. picks.blurb: Week 6 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Cowboys and Packers had much different results last week - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers take 3-0 NLCS lead WNBA All-Defensive first team Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Caleb's return won't solve it all Frank Schwab Senior writer Thu, October 15, 2026 at 2:37 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads One week can change the entire perception of an NFL team — sometimes that's good, sometimes it's not. The Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers were both 2-2 coming into last week's games. The Cowboys weren't considered a Super Bowl contender, but they were at least looking OK — especially in a bad NFC East — with a home game against the winless Buccaneers coming up. The Packers had played so poorly through four weeks that they were home underdogs to the Bears for the first time in 20 years , even though Chicago was starting its backup quarterback. The Cowboys and Packers come into Week 6's Sunday night game with their seasons flipped around. The Cowboys looked horrible against the Buccaneers, losing to an undrafted rookie quarterback in Jalon Daniels. The defensive problems finally got to a point in which the Cowboys hired longtime NFL defensive coordinator Mike Pettine as a senior defensive assistant and said defensive coordinator Christian Parker will now call plays from the press box. There's always some angst in Dallas because of the attention on the Cowboys all the time, but it's not like the defensive problems are made up. Dallas was last in defensive DVOA last season and they're last so far this season. Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Basketball league for the 2026-27 NBA season Meanwhile, the talk of Matt LaFleur being on the hot seat seems like it was a lot longer than a week ago. The best way to gain back the confidence of Packers fans is to blow out the Bears, and the Packers did just that. They blasted Chicago, 31-7, with Jordan Love embarrassing the Bears defense with his deep passing and Green Bay shutting down everything Chicago's offense wanted to do. After not playing a good game through four weeks, the Packers played a great game in Week 5. That makes Week 6 hard to figure out. Do the Cowboys rebound or is the defense simply unfixable? What's the real Packers team — the one that couldn't run the ball, couldn't protect Love and had a below-average defense through four games, or the one we saw Sunday? The Packers are small favorites Sunday night, indicating the oddsmakers don't have a lot of confidence in them still. But it's tougher to bank on the Cowboys' defense. Packers -1.5 is the pick , though it could all look different for both teams next week. That's how the NFL goes. The Green Bay Packers' MarShawn Lloyd celebrates a touchdown with the fans at Lambeau Field last week. (AP Photo/Nam Huh) Here are the rest of the picks against the spread for Week 6 of the NFL season: Seahawks (-2.5) over Broncos Not all is great for the defending champs, who can't run the ball and still don't have an offensive option other than Jaxon Smith-Njigba. But they've been far better than the Broncos, who were on their way to losing to the winless and injury-plagued Chargers before saving themselves with a fourth-quarter rally. The matchup of Seattle's defense against an aimless Broncos offense is enough to take the Seahawks. Jaguars (-2.5) over Texans A bit of a weird line. The Jaguars are 4-1 and while last week's miracle win over the Eagles wasn't great, they do look like a legitimate contender in the AFC. The Texans are 1-4 and their lone win came against the 0-5 Titans. And yet, in a neutral site game — if either team has the edge it's Jacksonville, who does the London trip every season and stayed overseas after playing there last week — the Jaguars aren't even giving a full field goal. Yes it's a desperate Houston team with a very good defense, but it's not a lot of respect for the Jaguars. Falcons (+1.5) over Bears It appears Michael Penix Jr. and Caleb Williams will start, which should make for an entertaining game. The big question for this one will be what to make of the Bears defense. In Week 1 and 5 they gave up 68 combined points. From Weeks 2-4 they allowed 28 points. The hot stretch in the middle could have come from facing three bad offenses (Vikings without Kyler Murray in bad weather, Eagles, Jets) instead of the Panthers and Packers, their other two opponents who both scored more than 30 points. The Falcons are a good offense with Penix, so points should be coming. Browns (+5.5) over Ravens The Ravens should have confidence after beating the Falcons without Lamar Jackson last week. However, a Tyler Huntley offense still isn't one I'm comfortable laying 5.5 points with on the road. Buccaneers (+2.5) over Steelers Metrics like DVOA and net EPA per play say these teams are practically even. The Buccaneers have the rest advantage, having played last Thursday night, and the Steelers are 0-2 on the road (3-0 at home). Daniels could be exposed by the best defense he's faced, but it's also not the intimidating Steelers defense from recent years. Patriots (-7.5) over Jets The Patriots are officially warmed up. The start to the season was lackluster, but Drake Maye is coming off two good games in a row. The Jets are better than some expected, but they're facing a team that has its season back on track and wants to keep that going. Bet the New England Patriots to cover the spread at sportsbooks Giants (+1.5) over Saints It's hard to buy the Giants. There's no evidence they're a good team despite their 3-1-1 record. But it's not like there are any signs that the Saints are much better. New Orleans is 30th in DVOA ahead of only the hopeless Titans and Dolphins. Anything can happen when Jameis Winston is starting at quarterback, good or bad — good luck predicting it. Panthers (-1) over Eagles It's weird to see the Panthers favored at Philadelphia (though some books have the Eagles as a small favorite). But to this point, Carolina has been the far better team. Also, they're coming off a bye while the Eagles come right off a flight from London, where they took a horrific loss after kicking a go-ahead field goal with eight seconds left. Colts (-7) over Titans The Titans should be very happy the Dolphins exist, or else there would be even more talk about how bad they are. Indianapolis hasn't been great, either, but it's just too difficult to take the Titans right now. Cardinals (+12.5) over Rams It's quite possible the Rams take out their frustrations on the Cardinals. Los Angeles is 2-3, but the schedule has been tough and it starts to ease up with a game against Arizona, which just got throttled by the Lions. The Cardinals seem to be running out of steam after looking decent to start the season. Still, 12.5 points is a lot considering the Rams haven't looked great yet, and Arizona can move the ball, especially in garbage time. Raiders (+5.5) over Bills The Bills are coming off an emotional, difficult overtime win against the Rams on Monday night. They are the better team, but that's a tough situational spot, and the Raiders are not as bad as they looked last week against the Patriots. Let's give Vegas one more shot to show that 3-0 start wasn't fraudulent. Chiefs (-8) over Chargers The Chargers aren't just bad, they're injured. They held their own against the Broncos last week, but that probably says more about Denver. This season is already ugly for Los Angeles and it's not going to get much better. Commanders (+7.5) over 49ers If the Commanders aren't completely downtrodden after one of the dumbest endings in recent NFL history last week, in which they casually watched the final minute of overtime run out without getting a field-goal attempt, then this seems like too many points. The 49ers have played very well on both sides of the ball (the defense has been a great surprise), but there is some danger of a letdown after winning at Seattle. Take the points and hope last week's fiasco doesn't still linger for Washington. Last week: 5-9-1 Season to date: 34-43-2

away.headline: Dallas Cowboys Could Bench DaRon Bland to Avoid Paying Massive Injury Guarantees
away.blurb: As pointed out by ESPN's Bill Barnwell, the Cowboys would be in a frustrating financial hole if Bland were to suffer an injury this season. "The Cowboys don't want to be on the hook for that money, so it would hardly be a surprise if they took Bland out of the lineup altogether once (Cobie) Durant and (Joey) Porter Jr. are back on the field to avoid triggering those guarantees, which would happen if Bland suffers a significant injury," Barnwell wrote. The Cowboys are also still figuring out exactly what they have in Shavon Revel Jr., who impressed during training camp but has had his own share of struggles this season. From being a fifth-round pick to making NFL history, Dallas Cowboys cornerback DaRon Bland deserves a ton of credit for the career he's made for himself. However, the magic from his record-setting 2023 season has quickly faded. Despite signing a four-year, $90 million contract extension last August, Bland has become a liability this season on a Dallas defense that already has enough problems to deal with. Bland hasn't had an interception since Week 7 of last season. And if he's not jumping routes and running it back for a touchdown -- something he's done six times in his career -- Bland is getting burned down the field for huge gains. As a result of his fading production and hefty contract, the Cowboys face an interesting dilemma when it comes to how they handle Bland's involvement in the defense moving forward in order to help themselves both on the field and in the bank. Cowboys Would Owe DaRon Bland $13 Million Due to Injury Dallas would owe Bland $13 million in guaranteed money if he suffers "a significant injury." Should he stay healthy, the Cowboys would avoid having to pay up. This situation makes it perfectly reasonable for the Cowboys to bench Bland moving forward. Until he proves he can produce at the level that his contract commands, Dallas faces a lose-lose situation: continue to suffer on defense while running the risk of owing Bland millions in injury guarantees. If the Cowboys are going to be awful on defense, they might as well do it with cornerbacks that won't put them in a tough spot financially. Cowboys Have More Reasonable Options to Work With When everyone is healthy, Dallas has multiple options that certainly feel like an upgrade from the current version of Bland. The Cowboys signed former Los Angeles Rams cornerback Cobie Durant this season before making the blockbuster deal for former Pittsburgh Steelers star Joey Porter Jr. earlier this month. And on top of that, Dallas has versatile defensive back Caleb Downs, who brings a bit of everything as a slot corner or a safety. It's hard to imagine Bland being outright ruled inactive for Week 6's matchup against the Green Bay Packers but the Cowboys could certainly benefit by slowing decreasing his snap count as the season goes on. away.headline: Cowboys Injury Updates: CeeDee Lamb, Tyler Guyton, Joey Porter Jr.
away.blurb: CeeDee Lamb, Tyler Guyton Return After Injury Scares Lamb was hit on the same quad he took a hit to the week before, and it became painful, Schottenheimer said. Lamb exited with 8:32 remaining in the fourth quarter, was listed as questionable to return, and was back on the field on the same drive. He finished with 2 catches for 9 yards on 5 targets and played 34 of the Cowboys’ 60 offensive snaps. Cornerback DaRon Bland played all 72 defensive snaps with Porter out. “It affects us too much. A little bit, just missing a guy. You always wanna have everybody there, so. And to have a lot of guys hurt right now. So it hurts a little bit,” Bland said. “But we still had to go out there and perform.” Safety Alijah Clark left in the second quarter with a hamstring injury and was ruled out in the third quarter. Cornerback Shavon Revel was hurt on a third-quarter play and returned early in the fourth quarter. ‘Everything Still Out In Front Of Us’: Dallas Cowboys 1.5 Games Back As NFC East Goes Winless In Week 5 Cowboys Injury Updates: CeeDee Lamb, Tyler Guyton, Joey Porter Jr. Home ARLINGTON, Texas — Dallas Cowboys receiver CeeDee Lamb and left tackle Tyler Guyton both left Thursday night’s 24-16 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers with injuries and returned, and cornerback Joey Porter Jr. was inactive after falling ill at AT&T Stadium. Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer gave initial updates after the game. Four days earlier, Lamb set a career high with 17 catches for 189 yards and caught the go-ahead 12-yard touchdown with 40 seconds left in a 34-30 win over the Houston Texans . Guyton’s X-rays looked good, Schottenheimer said, but the Cowboys will run more tests on his back. Guyton played 52 offensive snaps, 87% of the total. Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones said he did not know the seriousness of Guyton’s back strain, but that Guyton came back in at the end. Joey Porter Jr. Becomes ‘Very, Very Sick’ Before Kickoff Porter was a late scratch, and Schottenheimer said the decision came after the trainers went to the coaches before the game. “Unique thing. Came to the stadium and he wasn’t feeling very well. And trainers came to us, said it got significantly worse after we treated him,” Schottenheimer said. “He just wasn’t feeling good. And the decision was made that he wasn’t going to be able to play, as he was very, very sick.” Jones said Porter had flu symptoms and could not keep his food down. Dallas acquired Porter in a trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers last week, and Thursday was supposed to be his second game with the Cowboys, The Associated Press reported. DaRon Bland, Shavon Revel Among Cowboys Secondary Updates Receiver Jonathan Mingo was on the injury report entering the game, and Schottenheimer said a lot of people have had little things. Mingo played and caught 2 passes for 20 yards. Revel said after the game that he took a shot before kickoff and feels great. home.headline: Micah Parsons provides promising injury update for Packers fans
home.blurb: Micah Parsons, out since last December with a torn ACL, is nearing his comeback for the Packers as they look to bounce back from a slow start in the NFC North, winners of two games in a row. Around 9.5 months after his surgery last December, Parsons is nearing a return, but it won't come in Week 6 against his former Cowboys squad. He has yet to return to practice, and remains on Green Bay's PUP list as the team waits for him to be medically cleared. But it shouldn't be too long before that happens. "The biggest thing that people worried about with me, they're like, 'Man, why ain't he back yet?'" Parsons said. "If the Super Bowl was this week, I'm playing in the Super Bowl. But it's just about me making sure I have all the small things fixed first. What a lot of people don't figure out is it's not just the ACL. It's like, why did the ACL happen? What was weak? Because it all works together. It's a chain. And throughout the history of ACL, they notice if you come back early, there tends to be an overcompensation injury on the other side." Previously, he said he thought a return to face the Cowboys in Week 6 was "realistic," but it won't materialize as hoped. It won't be long before one of the NFL's premiere pass rushers is back on the field. Parsons provided the latest update on his timeline on his podcast recently, saying he's in the final stages of making sure his knee will hold up. Here's what Parsons said about his injury outlook. MORE: The Sporting News' latest 2027 NFL Mock Draft Micah Parsons provides injury update Parsons said on the latest episode of his podcast, "The Edge With Micah Parsons," that if it was a do-or-die game, he'd be ready to play, but has preferred to play it safe with his longer timeline. The star pass rusher said he wants to make sure he's fully at 100% before he returns. "It's like, what's the point of getting me back for four weeks and then next thing you know, my groin [is] bothering me," Parsons said. "So many people wanted me to be back for that game to make the game bigger than what it was," Parsons said on his podcast. "It's just another 'Sunday Night Football' game between two good teams. It's not about me. I think that probably let people down. 'Oh, Micah, he's gonna want to be back for the Dallas game.' No, I'm in that phase of life where I just want to be healthy again. That's it." For now, Parsons is waiting to be cleared so he can begin his ramp up to play. It won't be happening this week, but soon, the Packers will be getting a game-changing weapon back for their defense.
