picks.blurb: Commanders vs. 49ers bold predictions for Week 6 Monday Night Football - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers take 3-0 NLCS lead WNBA All-Defensive first team Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Caleb's return won't solve it all Commanders vs. 49ers bold predictions for Week 6 Monday Night Football Steven Bisig-Imagn Images Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints Wed, October 14, 2026 at 1:54 AM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads While the Washington Commanders are likely playing with a lame-duck coach, the San Francisco 49ers will be without a key defender. These teams, going in different directions, will meet in Week 6 on Monday Night Football, and here are bold predictions for the contest. Still reeling from a last-second overtime mental meltdown in the 27-27 tie to the Giants, the Commanders carry a record of 1-3-1 and a heavy underdog role into this game. Meanwhile, the 49ers are flying high with a record of 5-0 on the season. They're coming off an exciting 32-29 win over the Seahawks, giving them firm control of the NFC West title chase. 49ers QB Brock Purdy will throw for 300 yards The Commanders have been good against the run this season, giving up only 95.4 yards per game. They will have a challenge against the 49ers' offense, who are No. 8 in rushing yards per game. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Look for the Commanders to slow, not stop, Christian McCaffrey. However, that opens things up for the 49ers' passing attack to hit high gear. The biggest problem the Commanders will have is Mike Evans. That's not a deep analysis. It's something every team faces when playing the 49ers. Purdy said Evans makes a big difference , according to ESPN. "He's a game changer," Purdy said after the win over the Seahawks. "True X receiver that, if you get the right look and stuff and you give him a chance, he can make defenses pay. "I thought today he did a great job with that, going up and getting the ball multiple times and just using his length and everything to create some separation. So as a quarterback, any time I have an (opportunity) to go to him, it always feels good." Evans doesn't shy away from the attention. And why should he? He's a future Hall of Famer. "I do feel like I'm one of the best receivers in the game," Evans said. "I got a big frame, so if you throw it around me, I'm going to do my best to try to make those contested grabs." The 49ers won't have Deebo Samuel, who suffered a hamstring injury against the Seahawks. That could allow the Commanders to focus more attention on Evans. But the 49ers still have threats, including George Kittle. And even Kittle has major respect for Evans, according to a post on X. "Mike Evans is really good at football," Kittle posted. 49ers TE George Kittle will have a season-high reception total Kittle's best game came in Week 3 against the Cardinals as he grabbed six passes for 82 yards and a pair of scores. Look for him to have a similar line against the Commanders with Samuel on the shelf. The 49ers have Kittle, Jordan Watkins, Brandin Cooks, and Jacob Cowing on the roster. And that's enough , said head coach Kyle Shanahan, according to ESPN. "I think we have enough," Shanahan said. "We've got three guys on practice squad also who can help. I mean, anytime you lose this number of guys, whether it's four guys or five guys, whatever it is, it's a huge challenge. But we do have guys in this building who can do it, and we'll always look." Commanders QB Jayden Daniels will finally cross 200-yard passing mark In three games this season, Daniels hasn't totaled over 200 yards passing. Look for that to change against the 49ers. It makes sense for the 49ers to focus defensively on keeping Daniels in check as a runner. He's coming off a game where he ran for 103 yards on nine carries and a pair of touchdowns. And look for the Commanders' game plan to lean more on the passing game than it has so far this season. Part of it will likely be from necessity as the Commanders figure to be chasing points throughout this game. Daniels has a lot to prove after his late-game blunder against the Giants. He has tried to own the situation , according to ESPN. "We have to stop the clock," Daniels said. "We have to know the situation. We have to relay that as an offense. It starts with everyone, top down. Ultimately, it's on me." A bounce-back game against the 49ers by Daniels won't help Quinn's future as head coach. But it would be an olive branch to Commanders' fans who are furious about Daniels' mental meltdown. Commanders WR Terry McLaurin will get a long TD Look for the Commanders to strike deep against the 49ers. McLaurin should be the beneficiary with a 40-plus-yard score. McLaurin hasn't been anything special from a fantasy perspective this season. He had catch totals of 2, 2, 6, and 4 in his first four games. He has 203 total yards and one touchdown. Those aren't WR1 numbers. He is playing like a pedestrian blob so far this season. And while he probably won't juice up those numbers much against the 49ers' tough defense, it's not out of the realm of possibility for him to get a deep ball. How big of an ask is a 40-yard TD strike between Daniels and McLaurin? Consider that Daniels' longest pass of the season is 33 yards. McLaurin's longest catch is 30 yards. Those numbers seem to belie the likelihood of a long hookup. However, the 49ers can't fear the deep ball because of this duo's modest production. And that's why there's a window of opportunity for a bomb. However, look for the Commanders to fall to 1-4-1 after this one. They don't have the roster to compete with the 49ers. That’s a big blow, considering Diggs has been Washington’s leading receiver to this point. The Commanders formally listed McLaurin as questionable Friday afternoon on the team’s official injury report. The veteran suffered a hamstring injury in the last practice before Washington played the Colts in London, which kept him from playing that Week 4 game . Adding to that trouble, safeties Percy Butler (hamstring) and Tyler Owens (hamstring) are out of this game. Down three active safeties, Washington must elevate one to get through the game — they just added Darren Hall to the practice squad — where Quan Martin and Jeremy Reaves will play a ton. Defensive end Charles Omenihu (groin/ankle) is also out, which is a big blow to the defensive front. He has been integral to some generally solid run defense. Quarterback Marcus Mariota was ruled out earlier, so that was no shock. The Commanders opened 21-day practice windows for cornerback Trey Amos, defensive lineman Deatrich Wise and running back Jeremy McNichols and designated them questionable — that’s fairly common — but would have to add them to the active roster before playing. McLaurin participated in a limited capacity on Friday, but Diggs did not. Both wideouts are dealing with hamstring injuries. If McLaurin and Diggs are both out, Washington will be left with Dyami Brown, Antonio Williams, Treylon Burks, and Luke McCaffrey as its only healthy receivers. Losing Jaxson Dart and Brian Burns, among others, for the season was a devastating blow, but the G-Men still have enough healthy talent on both sides of the ball to remain competitive, especially in a wide-open NFC East. With key commanders missing from the lineup, the Giants have an important advantage in what has become a crucial game in the NFC East title race. Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs headline Commanders' injury report vs. Giants Daniels was a full participant in Commanders practice on both Wednesday and Thursday. Barring an unexpected change over the weekend, he should be able to play for the first time since injuring his elbow in Week 2. Of course, the Giants have some important injuries of their own. Braxton Berrios is now set to miss the season with a foot injury. Chauncey Golston's neck injury could leave New York thin on the edge, and safety Jason Pinnock is dealing with a concussion. But in terms of new names popping up on the injury report, the Giants certainly have the advantage in this game. Commanders' injury report gives Giants a clear advantage in Week 5 The Giants' secondary hasn't been stellar this season. The pass defense has been average in most categories and has been torn apart by the most efficient passing offenses it has faced. But if Washington is without its top two wide receivers, New York's secondary should be able to take control of the game. Deonte Banks, who has been a full participant in practice this week , and Greg Newsome II can lock Brown and Burks down on the outside while Dru Phillips handles Williams in the slot. If the Giants limit the Commanders' rushing attack, which hasn't been particularly efficient this year, they can put this game away early.

By Michael Gallagher Sports Content Coordinator 0 Share Newsweek is a Trust Project member See more of our trusted coverage when you search. Prefer Newsweek on Google to see more of our trusted coverage when you search. The San Francisco 49ers have had arguably the worst injury luck of any team in the NFL this season. More than 15 players are currently on the reserve/injured list while a handful of others are expected to miss some time with their respective ailments. San Francisco’s defense has been hit particularly hard, and star edge-rusher Nick Bosa’s absence over the last few weeks has been noticeable. Keion White has done his part to pick up the slack, but the rest of San Francisco’s pass-rush has left much to be desired, which is why Kristopher Knox of Bleacher Report believes the 49ers should make an all-in move to upgrade the position. Knox recently suggested the 49ers execute a trade with the winless Los Angeles Chargers for Pro Bowler Khalil Mack. “Los Angeles fell to 0-5 on Sunday, while Mack continues to be a legitimate difference-maker,” Knox wrote . “… Mack is playing on a one-year deal and should be interested in playing for a team that could get him his first career playoff win. “.. Mack should be the top target for any team with Super Bowl aspirations that happens to need help rushing opposing passers. It'll be a fairly significant surprise if he remains in Los Angeles beyond next month's deadline.” Despite multiple reports indicating the Chargers would want a fifth-round pick in exchange for Mack, Knox suggested it could take at least a conditional 2027 fourth-round pick to get a deal finalized given the demand for strong pass-rushers from contending teams. Through five games this season, Mack has logged 14 pressures, eight hurries, five tackles for loss, three QB hits, and three sacks with a pass-rush win-rate of 9.5%, according to Pro Football Focus. Adding that kind of production opposite White would be a big boost for the 49ers in the interim, and once Bosa comes back, it would make SF’s pass-rush all the more dangerous come playoff time.

home.blurb: Super Bowl stock report for NFL Week 6: 49ers emerge as new favorites, Bears await Caleb Williams' return - CBS Sports site: media | arena: nfl | pageType: stories | section: | slug: super-bowl-stock-report-for-nfl-week-6 | sport: football | route: article_single.us | 6-keys: media/spln/nfl/reg/free/stories Skip to Main Content Close Menu All Sports Menu Sports Watch Fantasy Betting Featured NFL User Menu Settings Log Out Log In Sign Up Fantasy & Games See All ArrowForward # # LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Perhaps their seemingly never-ending ailments will catch up to them again, but the same could be said for any team in the league. It is time to simply enjoy what the 49ers are doing and stop worrying about their ability to stay healthy. Frankly, they might just win the Super Bowl regardless of who is available. Through five weeks, it feels like their year. Here is how the rest of the Super Bowl race shakes out as the season approaches Week 6. Stock down: Bears desperately await Caleb Williams' return Would the Chicago Bears be 5-0 if Caleb Williams did not get hurt in Week 2? Suppose he stays on the field for that critical fourth-quarter drive in the 9-3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings. He would have had at least two more looks at the end zone. If he were available in Week 5, the Bears probably would not throw three interceptions in a 31-7 rout at the hands of the bitter rival Green Bay Packers . That is all hypothetical, of course, but Williams' talent makes it fair to wonder. Instead, the Bears are two games back of the NFC North lead and stand in the middle of the conference's slog of three-win teams. They seek a rebound effort on the heels of the second-worst loss of Ben Johnson's head coaching career. That will be harder to obtain with edge rusher Montez Sweat out for two games for a violation of the NFL's performance-enhancing substances policy . The good news (and Chicago needs some right now) is that Williams is on track to play in Week 6 against the Atlanta Falcons . His hamstring strain is behind him, which cleared the way for a return to practice on Wednesday. Case Keenum and Tyson Bagent kept the ship afloat but had clear limitations — most notably in the frustrating loss to the Packers — whereas Williams seems to be blossoming into a top-tier quarterback capable of leading his team deep into the postseason. It was easy to sneer at the Pittsburgh Steelers in the offseason when they hired a past-his-prime coach, let Aaron Rodgers drag them along with his decision-making process as to whether to return for another year and got embarrassed by the Philadelphia Eagles on draft day. They say everything happens for a reason, and they might be onto something when it comes to the Steelers. All of those developments, somehow, seem to have played out perfectly.
